## Summary

**Right-click (MouseDown3Status) menu location and status:**

The menu is **completely defined inline** with `display-menu -O` (the `-O` flag makes it stay open after click release). The menu items match your screenshot exactly:
- Swap Left/Right (lines 63–64)

**No other files override or modify this menu** — all `menu-*.sh` scripts are for the **prefix+Space popup menu** (not right-click tabs), called from `executable_menu.sh`.

## Workmux Data Flow

**Config:** `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/workmux/config.yaml`  
**Status helper API:** `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh`  
**Manual clear helper:** `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/shell/38_workmux.sh` (the `wmclear` function)

**The flow:**

1. **workmux writes to per-window user-var** `@workmux_status` via:
   ```bash
   workmux set-window-status <state>  # state = working|waiting|done|clear
   # Internally: tmux set-option -w '@workmux_status' '<glyph>'
   ```

2. **Catppuccin theme reads and renders it** (`theme.catppuccin.conf`, lines 31–32):
   ```
   set -g @catppuccin_window_text ' #W#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}'
   ```
   Format string: `#W` (window name) + conditional `#{?@workmux_status, <emoji>,}` (append emoji if set, else empty)

3. **Claude Code + OpenCode hooks call** `workmux set-window-status`:
   - Claude: `dot_claude/modify_settings.json` (Stop / SubagentStop / UserPromptSubmit hooks)
   - OpenCode: `dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts` (vendored plugin)

4. **Public API for non-agent producers:** `dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh`
   ```bash
   tmux_status_set my_build 🔨              # set per-window var @my_build_status
   tmux_status_get my_build                 # read it
   tmux_status_clear my_build               # unset it
   tmux_status_clear_all my_build           # unset across all windows
   tmux_status_run my_build 🔨 ✅ ❌ -- cmd # run cmd with badges
   ```

5. **Manual clearing:** `wmclear` (38_workmux.sh, lines 39–73)
   ```bash
   wmclear           # clear current window's @workmux_status
   wmclear 5         # clear window 5's @workmux_status
   wmclear --all     # clear every window in the session
   ```

---

## Current Per-Window Variables

**Only `@workmux_status` is in active use** for per-window badges. No other per-window `@*_status` vars exist.

Global session vars (not per-window): `@catppuccin_status_*`, `@_status_left_*`, `@_status_right_*` (in `responsive.sh`), but these are **session-level**, not per-window.

---

## Design Conflicts / Overlap

**No conflicts** between your proposed additions and workmux:

1. **wmclear menu item**: Can coexist perfectly. It would call `tmux_status_clear workmux` (or `workmux set-window-status clear`) on the right-clicked window — the menu has `#{window_id}` available, so you can target it directly.

2. **Bookmark toggle icon** (`@bookmark_status` or `@pinned_status`): Can render **alongside** `@workmux_status` without overwriting it. Modify the theme format on lines 31–32 of `theme.catppuccin.conf`:
   ```
   ' #W#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}#{?@bookmark_status, #{@bookmark_status},}'
   ```
   Both glyphs render in sequence: `window 🤖 ⭐` (agent working + bookmarked).

**Naming convention:** Use the public API layer (60_tmux_status.sh). Call it with a name like `bookmark` or `pinned`:
```bash
tmux_status_set bookmark ⭐           # tag current window
tmux_status_get bookmark              # check if set
tmux_status_clear bookmark            # remove bookmark
```
This keeps the namespace tidy (`@<name>_status` everywhere) and lets you grep for "every status producer" with `tmux_status_list`.

Perfect. Now I have all the information. Let me compile my findings:

## Report: Workmux Per-Window Status Icon Flow & Manual Bookmark Integration

### A. **Current data flow**

The 🤖/💬/✅ status icon reaches the tmux status line through a 3-stage pipeline:

1. **Source (hooks)**: Claude Code's `Stop`/`SubagentStop`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`Notification` hooks fire and call:
   ```
   command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && workmux set-window-status <state> || true
   ```
   (from `dot_claude/modify_settings.json` lines 59, 70, 88, 98)

2. **Storage (tmux per-window user option)**: `workmux set-window-status` writes to the tmux **per-window user-option** named `@workmux_status` via the equivalent of:
   ```bash
   tmux set-option -w '@workmux_status' '🤖'  # (or 💬 / ✅)
   ```

3. **Render (theme format string)**: The catppuccin theme evaluates a **conditional expansion** in its window-text format:
   ```tmux
   set -g @catppuccin_window_text ' #W#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}'
   set -g @catppuccin_window_current_text ' #W#{?window_zoomed_flag, 󰊓 ,}#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}'
   ```
   (lines 31–32 of `theme.catppuccin.conf`)

   The `#{?@workmux_status, …, }` syntax means: "if `@workmux_status` is set, render ` #{@workmux_status}` (space + value); otherwise render nothing."

The POSIX shell helpers in `60_tmux_status.sh` (lines 68–107) wrap this with the canonical command pattern:
```bash
tmux set-option -w [-t TARGET] "@${_name}_status" "$_glyph"  # set
tmux set-option -w [-t TARGET] -u "@${_name}_status"        # unset
```

---

### B. **Per-window option naming: current & reserved**

**Currently in use:**
- `@workmux_status` — exclusive; reserved by the validation in `60_tmux_status.sh:53` (rejects names starting with `workmux*`)
- `@catppuccin_*` — theme variables (flavor, window text, styles, etc.); these are **global** options, not per-window
- `@theme_variant` — global, for theme selection

**Safe naming for your bookmark feature:**
The validation in `60_tmux_status.sh:47–64` enforces:
- Names must match `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+`
- Names starting with `workmux` are rejected
- Empty names are rejected

**Recommended name:** `@bookmark` or `@bookmark_status` (follows the `@<tool>_status` convention from line 451 of `workmux.md`). Alternatively: `@pinned`, `@manual_mark`, `@tag_status`. The validation will accept any of these since none start with `workmux`.

---

### C. **Status format combinability: yes, fully supported**

Both window-text format strings **support concatenating multiple conditionals**. The current theme already demonstrates the pattern (line 32):
```tmux
' #W#{?window_zoomed_flag, 󰊓 ,}#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}'
```

This chains two conditionals in sequence. To add your bookmark:
```tmux
set -g @catppuccin_window_text ' #W#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}#{?@bookmark, ★,}'
set -g @catppuccin_window_current_text ' #W#{?window_zoomed_flag, 󰊓 ,}#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}#{?@bookmark, ★,}'
```

Result: window shows `zsh 🤖 ★` when both agent and bookmark are set, `zsh 🤖` for agent-only, `zsh ★` for bookmark-only, `zsh` for neither.

---

### D. **Manual clear surface: yes, `wmclear` + generic helpers**

**Existing workmux-specific escape hatch:**
- `wmclear` — function in `38_workmux.sh:39–73` clears `@workmux_status` for current window, a specific window, or all windows in session
- Direct command: `workmux set-window-status clear` (calls `wmclear` for current window; prefers this to preserve workmux's internal agent state)

**Generic POSIX helpers for your bookmark:**
The `60_tmux_status.sh` module already exports:
```bash
tmux_status_set bookmark '★' [mysession:3]    # set bookmark on current or target window
tmux_status_clear bookmark [mysession:3]       # unset bookmark on current or target window
tmux_status_clear_all bookmark                 # unset across every session
tmux_status_list                               # audit all @*_status across all windows
tmux_status_get bookmark                       # read current window's bookmark value
```

No pre-existing shell alias or binding for `bookmark` yet—you'd add one (e.g., `bmtoggle`, `bmclear`), but the primitives are ready.

---

### E. **Hard rules from the 6-file invariant (from CLAUDE.md)**

The workmux integration spans exactly **6 surfaces**. Quoting the CLAUDE.md "Hard rules":

> Never run `workmux setup` on a managed machine (would write parallel hook entries); never flip `status_format: true` (fights catppuccin's window-text override); never drop the `command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && … || true` guard in Claude hooks (spams errors on fresh boxes); never drop explicit `set-window-status done` from `Stop`/`SubagentStop` (upstream only ever sets `working`, never clears — that's the by-design leak).

**Current state (verified):**
1. ✅ `status_format: false` in `dot_config/workmux/config.yaml:26` — lock this in
2. ✅ `command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && … || true` guards present on all 4 hook entries (`modify_settings.json:59, 70, 88, 98`)
3. ✅ Both `Stop` and `SubagentStop` hooks call `set-window-status done` (`modify_settings.json:88, 98`)
4. ✅ `workmux setup` is **never** run—all hooks are vendored into chezmoi

**Safe additions for your manual-bookmark menu:**

Hand-rolled tmux commands in a menu binding (e.g., in `menu-agents.sh` or a new `menu-bookmarks.sh`) are 100% safe as long as they:

1. **Call `tmux_status_set bookmark …` or raw `tmux set-option -w @bookmark …`** instead of touching `@workmux_status`
2. **Never flip `status_format: true`** (don't modify workmux config)
3. **Never call `workmux setup`** (don't invite parallel hook rewrites)
4. **Append your conditional ONLY to the catppuccin format strings**, not to workmux's auto-manager (which is disabled)
5. **Preserve the `command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1` guard** if you call workmux from hooks (not needed for menu bindings, which run interactively in tmux)

The `60_tmux_status.sh` validation **already reserves** `workmux*` prefixes, so collision is impossible by design.

1	# ~/.config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh
2	# Source: dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh (managed by chezmoi)
3	#
4	# Generic per-window tmux status badge helpers — POSIX, sourced by both
5	# zsh and bash. Thin convenience layer over the same primitive workmux
6	# uses (`tmux set-option -w '@<name>_status' '<glyph>'`), so any script /
7	# hook / cron job / build watcher can tag its tmux window without
8	# pulling in workmux.
9	#
10	# Why a shared layer (not in 38_workmux.zsh): these helpers don't need
11	# any zsh feature, and the most common consumers (build scripts, deploy
12	# hooks, CI wrappers) tend to be `#!/bin/bash` or `#!/bin/sh`. Putting
13	# them in dot_config/shell/ means they Just Work from any shell.
14	#
15	# Companion: docs/tools/workmux.md → "Reusing the per-window status
16	# mechanism (without workmux)" for design rationale, the lifecycle hard
17	# rules, and the build-watcher worked example.
18	#
19	# Quick reference:
20	#
21	#   tmux_status_set my_build 🔨           # tag current window
22	#   tmux_status_set my_build 🔨 mysess:3  # tag specific window
23	#   tmux_status_get my_build              # read current window
24	#   tmux_status_clear my_build            # unset (current window)
25	#   tmux_status_clear my_build mysess:3   # unset specific window
26	#   tmux_status_clear_all my_build        # unset across every session
27	#   tmux_status_list                      # list every @*_status user-var
28	#   tmux_status_run my_build 🔨 ✅ ❌ -- npm run build
29	#                                         # set 🔨, run cmd, set ✅/❌
30	#                                         # by exit code, auto-clear on
31	#                                         # signal trap
32	#
33	# Naming convention: pass the LOGICAL name without `@` or `_status`
34	# suffix — these helpers add the `@<name>_status` wrapper. So
35	# `tmux_status_set my_build 🔨` writes `@my_build_status`. This keeps
36	# the user-var namespace tidy (`@<tool>_status` everywhere) and lets
37	# you grep for "every status producer" with `tmux_status_list`.
38	
39	# Skip silently if tmux isn't on PATH (cron, headless SSH, fresh box
40	# pre-ansible). Producers can call these unconditionally.
41	command -v tmux >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
42	
43	# Internal: validate name (alphanumeric + underscore + dash, no `@` /
44	# `_status` since we add them). Returns 0 if valid, 1 if not (with
45	# stderr diagnostic). Empty name is rejected. Names starting with
46	# `workmux` are reserved to avoid clobbering workmux's own user-var.
47	_tmux_status_validate_name() {
48	    if [ -z "${1:-}" ]; then
49	        printf 'tmux_status: name argument is required\n' >&2
50	        return 1
51	    fi
52	    case "$1" in
53	        workmux*)
54	            # shellcheck disable=SC2016 # Backticks here are literal Markdown-style code spans, not command substitution.
55	            printf 'tmux_status: name "%s" reserved (workmux owns @workmux_status). Use `workmux set-window-status` for the agent path.\n' "$1" >&2
56	            return 1
57	            ;;
58	        *[!A-Za-z0-9_-]*)
59	            printf 'tmux_status: name "%s" must be [A-Za-z0-9_-]+\n' "$1" >&2
60	            return 1
61	            ;;
62	    esac
63	    return 0
64	}
65	
66	# tmux_status_set <name> <glyph> [target]
67	#   target defaults to current window (`tmux display -p '#{session_name}:#{window_index}'`)
68	tmux_status_set() {
69	    _tmux_status_validate_name "${1:-}" || return 1
70	    if [ $# -lt 2 ]; then
71	        printf 'tmux_status_set: usage: tmux_status_set <name> <glyph> [target]\n' >&2
72	        return 1
73	    fi
74	    _name="$1"
75	    _glyph="$2"
76	    _target="${3:-}"
77	    if [ -n "$_target" ]; then
78	        tmux set-option -w -t "$_target" "@${_name}_status" "$_glyph" 2>/dev/null
79	    else
80	        tmux set-option -w "@${_name}_status" "$_glyph" 2>/dev/null
81	    fi
82	}
83	
84	# tmux_status_get <name> [target]
85	#   prints the glyph (or empty string + non-zero exit if unset)
86	tmux_status_get() {
87	    _tmux_status_validate_name "${1:-}" || return 1
88	    _name="$1"
89	    _target="${2:-}"
90	    if [ -n "$_target" ]; then
91	        tmux show-options -wv -t "$_target" "@${_name}_status" 2>/dev/null
92	    else
93	        tmux show-options -wv "@${_name}_status" 2>/dev/null
94	    fi
95	}
96	
97	# tmux_status_clear <name> [target]
98	tmux_status_clear() {
99	    _tmux_status_validate_name "${1:-}" || return 1
100	    _name="$1"
101	    _target="${2:-}"
102	    if [ -n "$_target" ]; then
103	        tmux set-option -w -t "$_target" -u "@${_name}_status" 2>/dev/null
104	    else
105	        tmux set-option -w -u "@${_name}_status" 2>/dev/null
106	    fi
107	}
108	
109	# tmux_status_clear_all <name>
110	#   walk every window in every session, unset @<name>_status
111	tmux_status_clear_all() {
112	    _tmux_status_validate_name "${1:-}" || return 1
113	    _name="$1"
114	    tmux list-windows -aF '#{session_name}:#{window_index}' 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r _w; do
115	        tmux set-option -w -t "$_w" -u "@${_name}_status" 2>/dev/null
116	    done
117	}
118	
119	# tmux_status_list
120	#   show every @*_status user-var across every window (read-only audit)
121	tmux_status_list() {
122	    tmux list-windows -aF '#{session_name}:#{window_index} #{window_name}' 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r _line; do
123	        _w="${_line%% *}"
124	        # Pull every option starting with @ on this window, filter to *_status
125	        tmux show-options -w -t "$_w" 2>/dev/null \
126	            | awk -v w="$_line" '/^@[A-Za-z0-9_-]+_status / {print w "  " $0}'
127	    done
128	}
129	
130	# tmux_status_run <name> <working_glyph> <ok_glyph> <fail_glyph> -- <cmd> [args...]
131	#   Run a command, badge the window with `working_glyph` while it runs,
132	#   then `ok_glyph` on success or `fail_glyph` on failure. Traps INT /
133	#   TERM / HUP to clear the badge instead of leaking on Ctrl+C.
134	#
135	#   Example:
136	#     tmux_status_run my_build 🔨 ✅ ❌ -- npm run build
137	#     tmux_status_run deploy   🚀 🟢 🔴 -- ./deploy.sh prod
138	tmux_status_run() {
139	    _tmux_status_validate_name "${1:-}" || return 1
140	    if [ $# -lt 6 ]; then
141	        printf 'tmux_status_run: usage: tmux_status_run <name> <working> <ok> <fail> -- <cmd> [args...]\n' >&2
142	        return 1
143	    fi
144	    _name="$1"
145	    _working="$2"
146	    _ok="$3"
147	    _fail="$4"
148	    shift 4
149	    if [ "${1:-}" != "--" ]; then
150	        # shellcheck disable=SC2016 # Backticks are literal in the diagnostic message.
151	        printf 'tmux_status_run: missing `--` separator before command\n' >&2
152	        return 1
153	    fi
154	    shift
155	    if [ $# -eq 0 ]; then
156	        # shellcheck disable=SC2016 # Backticks are literal in the diagnostic message.
157	        printf 'tmux_status_run: no command after `--`\n' >&2
158	        return 1
159	    fi
160	
161	    # Capture target ONCE up front — if `cmd` happens to switch tmux
162	    # window, we still want the badge to land on the window the user
163	    # invoked from.
164	    _target=$(tmux display -p '#{session_name}:#{window_index}' 2>/dev/null)
165	    [ -z "$_target" ] && _target=""
166	
167	    # Trap so Ctrl+C / kill doesn't leak the working glyph forever.
168	    # Use a trap that clears, then re-raises the signal default for
169	    # correct exit semantics.
170	    trap '_tmux_status_run_trap "$_name" "$_target"' INT TERM HUP
171	
172	    tmux_status_set "$_name" "$_working" "$_target"
173	    "$@"
174	    _rc=$?
175	    if [ $_rc -eq 0 ]; then
176	        tmux_status_set "$_name" "$_ok" "$_target"
177	    else
178	        tmux_status_set "$_name" "$_fail" "$_target"
179	    fi
180	
181	    trap - INT TERM HUP
182	    return $_rc
183	}
184	
185	# Internal: trap helper for tmux_status_run. Clears the badge then
186	# re-raises the signal so the calling shell sees correct $? / exit code.
187	_tmux_status_run_trap() {
188	    tmux_status_clear "$1" "$2" 2>/dev/null
189	    trap - INT TERM HUP
190	    # Re-raise INT (most common case); for TERM/HUP we just let the
191	    # shell continue — calling scripts can decide what to do via $?.
192	    kill -INT $$ 2>/dev/null
193	}

1	#!/bin/sh
2	# chezmoi modify_ script: hook-aware deep-merge of a managed overlay into
3	# ~/.claude/settings.json.
4	#
5	# Why hook-aware? Claude Code rewrites this file at runtime AND CodeIsland
6	# (https://github.com/wxtsky/CodeIsland, macOS notch HUD) auto-installs its
7	# own entries into hooks.Notification / hooks.PermissionRequest / hooks.Stop
8	# / hooks.PreToolUse / etc. workmux's `wm setup` ALSO writes Stop /
9	# UserPromptSubmit / Notification hook entries (see docs/tools/workmux.md
10	# → "Claude leak"). A naive `jq '. * $overlay'` deep-merge replaces arrays
11	# wholesale, so declaring our notify.sh hook in the overlay would silently
12	# delete every CodeIsland / workmux entry on each `chezmoi apply` (and the
13	# tools would re-install on next launch — endless ping-pong).
14	#
15	# How: For all keys EXCEPT .hooks, do the normal recursive object merge.
16	# For .hooks.<event> arrays, additively merge — append overlay entries that
17	# aren't already present (matched by .hooks[0].command), preserving every
18	# entry the live file already contains. This lets our overlay enforce
19	# notify.sh + workmux status updates while CodeIsland / workmux setup /
20	# any other tool freely manage their own parallel entries in the same
21	# event arrays.
22	#
23	# Workmux integration: We declare the workmux Stop / SubagentStop /
24	# UserPromptSubmit / Notification hooks here directly so they're enforced
25	# on every chezmoi apply WITHOUT requiring users to also run `wm setup`.
26	# The `command -v workmux` guard lets the hook no-op silently on machines
27	# where workmux isn't installed yet (fresh box, Linux without ansible run,
28	# etc.). This patches Claude's by-design 🤖-leak: Anthropic's Stop hook
29	# fires on every turn end, but workmux's `working` state never auto-clears
30	# without an explicit `done` set.
31	#
32	# To manage an additional hook event: add it to $overlay.hooks below.
33	# To manage an additional non-hook key: add it to $overlay.
34	# Requires: jq (installed by the `base` ansible role). On a fresh-box first
35	# apply, jq isn't yet installed; this script falls back to passing the live
36	# file through unchanged. See pitfalls/modify-script-jq-bootstrap-cycle.md.
37	#
38	# See: docs/tools/agent-overlays.md → "CodeIsland integration".
39	set -eu
40	
41	overlay=$(cat <<'JSON'
42	{
43	  "hooks": {
44	    "Notification": [
45	      {
46	        "matcher": "",
47	        "hooks": [
48	          {
49	            "type": "command",
50	            "command": "~/.claude/hooks/notify.sh"
51	          }
52	        ]
53	      },
54	      {
55	        "matcher": "",
56	        "hooks": [
57	          {
58	            "type": "command",
59	            "command": "command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && workmux set-window-status waiting || true"
60	          }
61	        ]
62	      }
63	    ],
64	    "UserPromptSubmit": [
65	      {
66	        "matcher": "",
67	        "hooks": [
68	          {
69	            "type": "command",
70	            "command": "command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && workmux set-window-status working || true"
71	          }
72	        ]
73	      }
74	    ],
75	    "Stop": [
76	      {
77	        "hooks": [
78	          {
79	            "type": "command",
80	            "command": "~/.claude/hooks/notify.sh"
81	          }
82	        ]
83	      },
84	      {
85	        "hooks": [
86	          {
87	            "type": "command",
88	            "command": "command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && workmux set-window-status done || true"
89	          }
90	        ]
91	      }
92	    ],
93	    "SubagentStop": [
94	      {
95	        "hooks": [
96	          {
97	            "type": "command",
98	            "command": "command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && workmux set-window-status done || true"
99	          }
100	        ]
101	      }
102	    ]
103	  },
104	  "enabledPlugins": {
105	    "pyright-lsp@claude-plugins-official": true,
106	    "claude-hud@claude-hud": true
107	  },
108	  "extraKnownMarketplaces": {
109	    "claude-hud": {
110	      "source": {
111	        "source": "github",
112	        "repo": "jarrodwatts/claude-hud"
113	      }
114	    }
115	  },
116	  "skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt": true,
117	  "permissions": {
118	    "defaultMode": "bypassPermissions"
119	  },
120	  "statusLine": {
121	    "type": "command",
122	    "command": "bash -c 'plugin_dir=$(ls -d \"${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}\"/plugins/cache/claude-hud/claude-hud/*/ 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -1); runtime=$(command -v bun 2>/dev/null || command -v node 2>/dev/null); [ -z \"$runtime\" ] && exit 0; rt=\"${runtime##*/}\"; if [ \"$rt\" = \"bun\" ]; then exec \"$runtime\" --env-file /dev/null \"${plugin_dir}src/index.ts\"; else exec \"$runtime\" \"${plugin_dir}dist/index.js\"; fi'"
123	  }
124	}
125	JSON
126	)
127	
128	base=$(cat)
129	[ -z "$base" ] && base='{}'
130	
131	# Cold-start fallback: jq is installed by the `base` ansible role, which
132	# runs AFTER this file-apply phase. Pass the live file through unchanged
133	# and warn — the next apply (after ansible) does the real merge.
134	if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
135	  printf '%s\n' "modify_settings.json: jq not found; passing live file through unchanged. Re-run \`chezmoi apply\` after the base ansible role installs jq." >&2
136	  printf '%s' "$base"
137	  exit 0
138	fi
139	
140	# Hook-aware merge:
141	#   1. Compute non-hook portion of overlay (everything except .hooks).
142	#   2. Deep-merge that into base normally: base * overlay_no_hooks.
143	#   3. For each event in overlay.hooks, append entries whose .hooks[0].command
144	#      isn't already represented in the live event array (by exact-string
145	#      command match on .hooks[0].command). Live entries are preserved
146	#      verbatim, and new overlay entries are added at the end.
147	printf '%s' "$base" | jq --argjson overlay "$overlay" '
148	  . as $base
149	  | ($overlay | del(.hooks)) as $non_hook_overlay
150	  | ($overlay.hooks // {}) as $overlay_hooks
151	  | ($base * $non_hook_overlay) as $merged
152	  | $merged
153	  | .hooks = (
154	      ($merged.hooks // {}) as $live_hooks
155	      | reduce ($overlay_hooks | to_entries[]) as $ev (
156	          $live_hooks;
157	          .[$ev.key] = (
158	            (.[$ev.key] // []) as $live_arr
159	            | ($live_arr | map(.hooks[0].command? // "")) as $live_cmds
160	            | $live_arr + (
161	                $ev.value
162	                | map(select(
163	                    (.hooks[0].command? // "") as $cmd
164	                    | ($cmd == "") or (($live_cmds | index($cmd)) == null)
165	                  ))
166	              )
167	          )
168	        )
169	    )
170	'
171

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Top-level tmux popup menu — invoked by `prefix + Space`.
3	#
4	# Why a script (not inline `display-menu` in keybindings.conf):
5	#   1. tmux's command parser stops at literal `;`, `{`, `}` even inside
6	#      nested quotes. With ~50 menu rows full of fzf binds and shell
7	#      one-liners, escaping became fragile and broke silently.
8	#   2. tmux `display-menu` does not paginate. If the menu is taller than
9	#      the terminal, the entire popup is suppressed with no error. By
10	#      generating the menu here we can read $TMUX client_height and
11	#      auto-trim low-frequency rows when small.
12	#   3. Submenus are normal `tmux display-menu` invocations from rows;
13	#      they don't share quoting context with the parent menu.
14	#
15	# Submenus live in sibling scripts:
16	#   menu-layouts.sh, menu-session.sh, menu-sesh.sh,
17	#   menu-popups.sh, menu-theme.sh, menu-system.sh, menu-agents.sh
18	#
19	# See: pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-parse-failure.md
20	
21	set -euo pipefail
22	
23	H=$(tmux display-message -p '#{client_height}')
24	DIR=~/.config/tmux
25	
26	# Tier 0: ALWAYS shown (highest frequency, ~7 rows + 2 separators)
27	declare -a tier0=(
28	  "Last window"  Tab "last-window"
29	  "Last pane"    P   "last-pane"
30	  ""             ""  ""
31	  "Choose win"   w   "choose-tree -Zw"
32	  "Choose sess"  s   "choose-tree -Zs"
33	  "Pane #s"      q   "display-panes -d 0"
34	  ""             ""  ""
35	  "Sesh picker"  g   "run-shell '$DIR/sesh-picker.sh'"
36	  "Lazygit"      G   "display-popup -E -w 90% -h 90% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' lazygit ' 'lazygit'"
37	)
38	
39	# Tier 1: shown when height >= 22 (adds new-window/split/zoom)
40	declare -a tier1=(
41	  ""             ""  ""
42	  "New window"   c   "new-window -c '#{pane_current_path}'"
43	  "Split |"      "|" "split-window -h -c '#{pane_current_path}'"
44	  "Split -"      "-" "split-window -v -c '#{pane_current_path}'"
45	  "Zoom"         z   "resize-pane -Z"
46	)
47	
48	# Tier 2: submenus + cheatsheet (always shown if Tier 1 is shown)
49	declare -a tier2=(
50	  ""             ""  ""
51	  "→ Layouts"    L   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-layouts.sh'"
52	  "→ Session"    S   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-session.sh'"
53	  "→ Sesh+"      E   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-sesh.sh'"
54	  "→ Agents"     A   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-agents.sh'"
55	  "→ Popups"     o   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-popups.sh'"
56	  "→ Theme"      T   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-theme.sh'"
57	  "→ System"     Y   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-system.sh'"
58	  ""             ""  ""
59	  "Cheatsheet"   "?" "display-popup -E -w 80% -h 80% -T ' tmux cheatsheet ' 'glow -p $DIR/cheatsheet.md 2>/dev/null || less $DIR/cheatsheet.md'"
60	  "Search keys"  "/" "run-shell -b ~/.tmux/plugins/tmux-fzf/scripts/keybinding.sh"
61	)
62	
63	rows=("${tier0[@]}")
64	if [ "$H" -ge 22 ]; then
65	  rows+=("${tier1[@]}" "${tier2[@]}")
66	elif [ "$H" -ge 14 ]; then
67	  rows+=("${tier2[@]}")
68	fi
69	
70	exec tmux display-menu -T "#[align=centre,bold]tmux (h=$H)" -x R -y P "${rows[@]}"
71
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# 38_workmux.sh - Workmux (`workmux` / `wm`) tmux + git-worktree orchestrator
2	# (shared bash + zsh). Moved from dot_config/zsh/tools/38_workmux.zsh; the
3	# only zsh-ism was `${(@f)$(cmd)}` (split-on-newlines flag), rewritten as a
4	# `while IFS= read -r` loop.
5	#
6	# https://workmux.raine.dev — github.com/raine/workmux
7	#
8	# Companion config: ~/.config/workmux/config.yaml (managed by chezmoi at
9	# dot_config/workmux/config.yaml). See docs/tools/workmux.md for the full
10	# story (worktrunk vs workmux split, status icon lifecycle, leak mitigation).
11	#
12	# Why a separate file from 37_worktrunk.{sh,zsh}: the two tools coexist
13	# (worktrunk = `wt` for git-worktree CLI / aliases, workmux = `wm` for status
14	# icons + dashboard + sidebar). Separate files keep the rationale + helpers
15	# per-tool and let users disable one independently.
16	
17	# Skip silently if not installed (Linux ansible install can fail offline,
18	# Cargo path may not be present, etc.)
19	command -v workmux &>/dev/null || return 0
20	
21	# ── Manual marker cleanup ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
22	#
23	# The `working` (🤖) status workmux sets is *sticky* — it never auto-clears
24	# on its own. `waiting` (💬) and `done` (✅) auto-clear when you focus the
25	# window, but `working` only goes away when:
26	#   1. The agent's plugin/hook explicitly calls `workmux set-window-status done`
27	#      (Claude Stop / OpenCode session.idle), OR
28	#   2. `workmux sidebar` is running and detects 10s of pane silence
29	#      (interrupted-agent detection), OR
30	#   3. You manually clear it.
31	#
32	# Path #1 fails when the agent is killed before its Stop/idle handler fires
33	# (Ctrl+C, terminal crash, OOM). Path #2 requires keeping a sidebar pane open.
34	# `wmclear` is the manual escape hatch.
35	#
36	# Without arg: clears the marker for the current tmux window.
37	# With arg:    `wmclear 5` clears window 5 in the current session.
38	# Pass `--all` to nuke every workmux marker in the current session.
39	function wmclear() {
40	    if [[ "$1" == "--all" ]]; then
41	        # Walk every window in the current session and unset the user-var.
42	        # Original zsh code used `windows=("${(@f)$(...)}")` to split command
43	        # output on newlines; the `while IFS= read -r` loop below is the
44	        # portable equivalent (works in bash + zsh).
45	        local sess
46	        sess=$(tmux display -p '#{session_name}' 2>/dev/null) || return 1
47	        local -a windows
48	        windows=()
49	        local w
50	        while IFS= read -r w; do
51	            [ -n "$w" ] && windows+=( "$w" )
52	        done < <(tmux list-windows -t "$sess" -F '#{window_index}' 2>/dev/null)
53	        for w in "${windows[@]}"; do
54	            tmux set-option -w -t "${sess}:${w}" -u '@workmux_status' 2>/dev/null
55	        done
56	        echo "Cleared @workmux_status on ${#windows[@]} windows in session $sess"
57	        return 0
58	    fi
59	
60	    if [[ -n "$1" ]]; then
61	        # Specific window: use workmux's own clear command (handles agent
62	        # state too, not just the tmux user-var)
63	        local sess win
64	        sess=$(tmux display -p '#{session_name}' 2>/dev/null) || return 1
65	        win="$1"
66	        tmux set-option -w -t "${sess}:${win}" -u '@workmux_status' 2>/dev/null
67	        echo "Cleared @workmux_status on ${sess}:${win}"
68	        return 0
69	    fi
70	
71	    # Current window: prefer workmux's clear so it also resets agent state
72	    workmux set-window-status clear 2>/dev/null
73	}
74	
75	# ── Sidebar daemon convenience ─────────────────────────────────────────────
76	#
77	# `workmux sidebar` is what enables the "interrupted agent" auto-clear (10s
78	# pane-silence heuristic). Without it, `working` markers leak forever on
79	# crashed agents. NOT auto-started here because it spawns a tmux pane and
80	# many users want to opt-in. Use `wmsb` to toggle.
81	alias wmsb='workmux sidebar'
82	
83	# ── Short aliases mirroring upstream's recommendation ──────────────────────
84	# README explicitly suggests `alias wm='workmux'`. The Linux ansible install
85	# also creates a `wm` symlink in ~/.local/bin so this alias is redundant on
86	# Linux, but on macOS Homebrew installs only `workmux`, so define it here.
87	if ! command -v wm &>/dev/null; then
88	    alias wm='workmux'
89	fi
90
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# Workmux — tmux + git-worktree orchestration with agent status icons
2	
3	[Workmux](https://workmux.raine.dev) (`workmux` / `wm`) is a CLI from
4	[raine/workmux](https://github.com/raine/workmux) that ties tmux windows,
5	git worktrees, and AI coding agents into one workflow. It coexists with
6	[`worktrunk`](worktrunk.md) (`wt`) in this repo — the two solve overlapping
7	problems but each has a unique killer feature, so we keep both managed.
8	
9	> **TL;DR**
10	> - `wt` = worktree CLI / aliases / `wt cc fix-x -- 'prompt'` per-branch
11	>   Claude launcher. See [worktrunk playbook](worktrunk.md).
12	> - `wm` = same worktree-launcher concept BUT also: 🤖/💬/✅ icons in tmux
13	>   window list, `wm dashboard` TUI, `wm sidebar` always-on status pane,
14	>   per-window status user-var (`@workmux_status`).
15	> - This repo auto-installs both, manages `wm`'s status hooks for Claude
16	>   Code + OpenCode so the icons work on every fresh box, and patches the
17	>   upstream by-design `working` (🤖) leak so it doesn't get stuck.
18	
19	## Table of Contents
20	
21	- [Why both wt and wm?](#why-both-wt-and-wm)
22	- [What this repo manages for you](#what-this-repo-manages-for-you)
23	- [Status icon mechanics](#status-icon-mechanics)
24	- [The 🤖-leak problem and how we fix it](#the--leak-problem-and-how-we-fix-it)
25	- [Self-managed status format](#self-managed-status-format)
26	- [Daily commands](#daily-commands)
27	- [Manual cleanup: `wmclear`](#manual-cleanup-wmclear)
28	- [Sidebar daemon (optional)](#sidebar-daemon-optional)
29	- [Adding a new agent](#adding-a-new-agent)
30	- [Reusing the per-window status mechanism (without workmux)](#reusing-the-per-window-status-mechanism-without-workmux)
31	  - [Shell helpers: `tmux_status_*`](#shell-helpers-tmux_status_)
32	- [Cross-references](#cross-references)
33	
34	---
35	
36	## Why both wt and wm?
37	
38	| Capability | `wt` (worktrunk) | `wm` (workmux) |
39	|---|---|---|
40	| Create worktree + branch + tmux pane | ✅ `wt switch -c -x claude feat` | ✅ `wm add feat` |
41	| Per-branch alias system | ✅ `[aliases]` in toml | ⚠️ named layouts only |
42	| Cleanup `merge`/`remove` lifecycle | ✅ | ✅ |
43	| Hooks (pre/post-start/merge/remove) | ✅ ten hook types | ✅ four hook types |
44	| Tmux window-status agent icon | ❌ no integration | ✅ `@workmux_status` |
45	| Always-visible status sidebar | ❌ | ✅ `wm sidebar` |
46	| Dashboard TUI (`d` for diff, `c` for commit) | ⚠️ interactive picker only | ✅ `wm dashboard` |
47	| Sandbox (Docker / Lima / Apple Container) | ❌ | ✅ |
48	| LLM commit messages | ✅ `wt merge` invokes LLM | ❌ |
49	| Auto-detected backend (kitty / wezterm / zellij) | ⚠️ tmux-only | ✅ multi-backend |
50	| Already in this repo | since 2026-04 | since 2026-05-11 |
51	
52	You don't have to use both. The split is:
53	
54	- **`wt cc <branch> -- 'prompt'`** stays the muscle-memory entry for
55	  parallel Claude/OpenCode in a worktree (worktrunk's alias engine is more
56	  expressive).
57	- **`wm` is what gives you the 🤖/💬/✅ icons** in the tmux window list, no
58	  matter which tool you used to spawn the agent. The icons come from
59	  workmux hooks installed in Claude/OpenCode that run regardless of which
60	  CLI you used to launch them.
61	- **`wm dashboard` / `wm sidebar`** for monitoring N parallel agents.
62	
63	If you only want one, drop `wt`'s aliases from
64	[`dot_config/worktrunk/config.toml`](../../dot_config/worktrunk/config.toml)
65	and use `wm add -x claude` in its place.
66	
67	## What this repo manages for you
68	
69	| File / setting | Path | Purpose |
70	|---|---|---|
71	| Binary install (macOS) | `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` (`workmux` in `homebrew:` list, `raine/workmux` tap) | `brew install workmux` on every macOS apply |
72	| Binary install (Linux) | `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` (workmux block) | Downloads `workmux-linux-{amd64,arm64}.tar.gz` from GitHub releases to `~/.local/bin/`; symlinks `wm -> workmux` |
73	| Global config | [`dot_config/workmux/config.yaml`](../../dot_config/workmux/config.yaml) | `nerdfont: false` + `status_format: false` (we manage the tmux format ourselves) |
74	| Tmux window format | [`dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf`](../../dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf) | Appends `#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}` to `@catppuccin_window_text` / `@catppuccin_window_current_text` |
75	| Claude hooks | [`dot_claude/modify_settings.json`](../../dot_claude/modify_settings.json) | Adds `Stop` / `SubagentStop` / `UserPromptSubmit` / `Notification` hooks calling `workmux set-window-status` |
76	| OpenCode plugin | [`dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts`](../../dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts) | Vendored copy of upstream plugin — listens to OpenCode events, calls `workmux set-window-status` |
77	| OpenCode plugin deps | [`dot_config/opencode/modify_package.json`](../../dot_config/opencode/modify_package.json) | jq-merges `@opencode-ai/plugin: 1.4.3` into existing `package.json` |
78	| Shell helpers | [`dot_config/zsh/tools/38_workmux.zsh`](../../dot_config/zsh/tools/38_workmux.zsh) | `wmclear` (manual marker reset), `wmsb` alias, `wm='workmux'` fallback alias |
79	
80	What is **NOT** managed (by design):
81	
82	- `wm setup` is not auto-run. It would write the same Claude/OpenCode hooks
83	  we already manage above, leading to duplicate entries (the hook-aware
84	  merger in `modify_settings.json` would deduplicate them but the cleaner
85	  path is to skip `wm setup` entirely on managed machines). On a fresh box
86	  the chezmoi layer installs everything `wm setup` would have done.
87	- `~/.config/workmux/state/` (per-machine runtime state — XDG state dir).
88	- `wm dashboard` color theme overrides — defaults are fine.
89	- Per-project `.workmux.yaml` — that lives in each project repo, not here.
90	
91	## Status icon mechanics
92	
93	Three states, three glyphs (defaults):
94	
95	| State | Glyph | Set by | Auto-clear behaviour |
96	|---|---|---|---|
97	| `working` | 🤖 | Agent processing a turn | ❌ **Sticky** — never auto-clears |
98	| `waiting` | 💬 | Permission prompt / question | ✅ Clears when window receives focus |
99	| `done` | ✅ | Turn finished gracefully | ✅ Clears when window receives focus |
100	| `clear` | (none) | Explicit unset | — |
101	
102	The mechanism: `workmux set-window-status <state>` writes to the tmux
103	**per-window user option** `@workmux_status` for the current window. Our
104	catppuccin format string appends `#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}`,
105	so any window with the option set renders the glyph after `#W`.
106	
107	Verify on a live tmux:
108	
109	```bash
110	# See which windows have the marker set
111	tmux list-windows -aF '#{session_name}:#{window_index} #{@workmux_status}'
112	
113	# Look at the format string our theme installed
114	tmux show -gv @catppuccin_window_text
115	# Expected: ' #W#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}'
116	```
117	
118	## The 🤖-leak problem and how we fix it
119	
120	`working` is **sticky by design** — it only transitions away when the agent
121	explicitly calls `set-window-status done` (or `clear`). When the agent dies
122	ungracefully (Ctrl+C, terminal crash, OOM, SSH disconnect), no `done` ever
123	fires and the 🤖 sticks forever.
124	
125	Worse for Claude specifically: upstream's default `wm setup` only installs
126	hooks that **set** `working` (`PostToolUse`, `UserPromptSubmit`) — there is
127	no `Stop` hook calling `set-window-status done`. Every Claude turn ends with
128	🤖 still showing. This is **by design** in upstream and was the root cause
129	of the [original investigation](../../pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md).
130	
131	This repo fixes both leak modes:
132	
133	1. **Claude `Stop` + `SubagentStop` hooks** — managed in
134	   [`dot_claude/modify_settings.json`](../../dot_claude/modify_settings.json).
135	   Every Claude turn end calls `workmux set-window-status done`, which
136	   immediately makes ✅ appear and then auto-clears on focus. Fixes the
137	   by-design leak.
138	
139	2. **OpenCode `session.idle` event handler** — vendored from upstream into
140	   [`dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts`](../../dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts).
141	   This works for graceful shutdowns. Crash/Ctrl+C still leaks.
142	
143	3. **Crash leak (any agent)** — three escape hatches:
144	   - `workmux sidebar` running anywhere → 10s pane-silence detection
145	     auto-downgrades stuck `working` to interrupted (released v0.1.99 +
146	     v0.1.163). See [Sidebar daemon (optional)](#sidebar-daemon-optional).
147	   - `wmclear` (this repo's helper) — manual reset. See
148	     [Manual cleanup](#manual-cleanup-wmclear).
149	   - `command -v workmux >/dev/null && workmux set-window-status clear` —
150	     raw command if you forget the alias.
151	
152	The `command -v workmux` guard in our Claude hooks means the hook silently
153	no-ops on a fresh machine where ansible hasn't run yet (or on a server
154	without workmux installed) — you'll see no errors in Claude's hook log.
155	
156	## Self-managed status format
157	
158	Workmux's default install (`wm setup`) modifies `window-status-format`
159	**per-tmux-session** the first time `wm` runs in that session. Three
160	problems with the default:
161	
162	1. **Per-session drift** — older tmux sessions that predate your last `wm`
163	   invocation never get the format. Reattach to one and the icons silently
164	   don't render.
165	2. **Invisible to chezmoi** — the format string lives in tmux's runtime,
166	   not in a config file we can diff.
167	3. **Conflicts with catppuccin's `@catppuccin_window_text` override** in
168	   this repo (catppuccin re-derives the format on every plugin run).
169	
170	Solution: set `status_format: false` in
171	[`dot_config/workmux/config.yaml`](../../dot_config/workmux/config.yaml) and
172	manage the format ourselves in
173	[`dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf`](../../dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf).
174	Both `@catppuccin_window_text` and `@catppuccin_window_current_text` get
175	the `#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}` suffix appended. The
176	conditional renders nothing when the user-var is unset, so windows without
177	agents look identical to before this change.
178	
179	## Daily commands
180	
181	The full upstream reference is at
182	[workmux.raine.dev](https://workmux.raine.dev). Quick crib for this repo:
183	
184	```bash
185	# Create a worktree + tmux window + Claude pane
186	wm add fix-login --prompt 'Login times out after 5min, fix to 24h'
187	
188	# Same but reuse if it exists
189	wm add fix-login -o
190	
191	# Three parallel agents, one per branch
192	wm add login-a --prompt 'Approach A' --background
193	wm add login-b --prompt 'Approach B' --background
194	wm add login-c --prompt 'Approach C' --background
195	
196	# Check status of every running agent
197	wm dashboard
198	# or compact CLI:
199	wm list
200	
201	# Always-on status sidebar (also enables 10s leak auto-clear)
202	wm sidebar
203	
204	# Jump to most recently finished/waiting agent
205	wm last-done
206	
207	# Merge into main and clean up worktree + branch + tmux window
208	wm merge
209	
210	# Just remove without merging
211	wm remove fix-login
212	```
213	
214	Aliases ([`dot_config/zsh/tools/38_workmux.zsh`](../../dot_config/zsh/tools/38_workmux.zsh)):
215	
216	| Alias | Expands to | Notes |
217	|---|---|---|
218	| `wm` | `workmux` | Defined as alias on macOS; symlink in `~/.local/bin` on Linux |
219	| `wmsb` | `workmux sidebar` | Toggle the sidebar |
220	| `wmclear` | (function — see below) | Manual marker reset |
221	
222	## Manual cleanup: `wmclear`
223	
224	```bash
225	# Clear the marker on the current window (calls workmux set-window-status clear)
226	wmclear
227	
228	# Clear marker on a specific window in current session
229	wmclear 5
230	
231	# Nuke every workmux marker in the current tmux session
232	wmclear --all
233	```
234	
235	Implementation lives in `dot_config/zsh/tools/38_workmux.zsh`. The single-
236	window form prefers `workmux set-window-status clear` so workmux's internal
237	agent-state is also reset; the bulk forms fall back to `tmux set-option -w
238	-u @workmux_status` which only clears the user-var.
239	
240	## Sidebar daemon (optional)
241	
242	Run `wm sidebar` (or `wmsb`) once per tmux session to spawn the sidebar
243	pane. Two side benefits beyond the visible status panel:
244	
245	1. **Interrupted-agent detection** — works only while sidebar is running.
246	   Watches each agent pane for output; after 10s of silence on a `working`
247	   agent, marks it interrupted and (per upstream v0.1.163+) downgrades the
248	   icon. Fixes the crash-leak with no manual cleanup.
249	2. **Cross-window status at a glance** — see all running agents and their
250	   git diff stats without `prefix + w`-ing through windows.
251	
252	Cost: one tmux pane (configurable width, default ~30 cols). Auto-resizes
253	on terminal resize. Toggle off with `wm sidebar` again.
254	
255	This repo deliberately does **NOT** auto-spawn the sidebar — too intrusive
256	for users who just want the icons. Add it manually to your tmux startup if
257	you want it everywhere:
258	
259	```bash
260	# Add to your ~/.tmux.conf.local or similar (NOT chezmoi-managed by default)
261	set-hook -g session-created 'run-shell "workmux sidebar 2>/dev/null || true"'
262	```
263	
264	## Adding a new agent
265	
266	Workmux supports Claude, OpenCode, Codex, Copilot CLI, Pi, and Gemini for
267	status tracking ([upstream support
268	matrix](https://workmux.raine.dev/guide/status-tracking#agent-support)).
269	Codex/Copilot/Pi don't have a `waiting` state due to upstream API limits.
270	
271	To add tracking for a new agent **on every machine** (not just one box):
272	
273	1. Read upstream's per-agent setup at
274	   [workmux.raine.dev/guide/status-tracking](https://workmux.raine.dev/guide/status-tracking)
275	   — typically a hook config in the agent's settings file.
276	2. Don't run `wm setup`. Instead vendor the hook config into this repo:
277	   - For agents that already have an overlay file (`dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl`,
278	     etc.), add the hook entries to that overlay's template so the
279	     hook-aware merger preserves user/runtime additions.
280	   - For agents without an overlay yet, model after
281	     [`dot_claude/modify_settings.json`](../../dot_claude/modify_settings.json)
282	     or [`dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts`](../../dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts).
283	3. Wrap the actual `workmux set-window-status` call with
284	   `command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && ... || true` so the hook no-ops
285	   on machines where workmux isn't installed yet.
286	 4. Update the table under [What this repo
287	    manages](#what-this-repo-manages-for-you) with the new file.
288	
289	## Reusing the per-window status mechanism (without workmux)
290	
291	The `@workmux_status` glyph is a thin wrapper over a generic tmux primitive:
292	**per-window user options + a conditional in `window-status-format`**. You
293	can use the same trick for ANY long-running thing whose state you want
294	glanceable in the tab bar — build watchers, test runners, deploy progress,
295	queue depth, alert badges, on-call rotation, anything. Workmux is one
296	producer; you can add more.
297	
298	### The primitive (3 moving parts)
299	
300	1. **Set** a per-window user option (any name starting with `@`):
301	   ```bash
302	   # Current window
303	   tmux set-option -w '@my_status' '🔨'
304	   # Specific window
305	   tmux set-option -w -t 'mysession:3' '@my_status' '⚠️'
306	   # Unset (clear)
307	   tmux set-option -w -u '@my_status'
308	   ```
309	
310	   …or use the **POSIX shell helpers** managed by this repo
311	   ([`dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh`](../../dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh)),
312	   which wrap the raw tmux calls with name validation, list/audit, and
313	   a `run` helper that traps Ctrl+C so badges don't leak. Both zsh and
314	   bash auto-source this file. See the [shell helpers reference
315	   below](#shell-helpers-tmux_status_) for the full API.
316	
317	   ```bash
318	   tmux_status_set my_build 🔨           # tag current window
319	   tmux_status_set my_build 🔨 mysess:3  # tag specific window
320	   tmux_status_clear my_build            # unset (current window)
321	   tmux_status_run my_build 🔨 ✅ ❌ -- npm run build
322	                                         # set 🔨, run cmd, set ✅/❌
323	                                         # by exit code, auto-clear on
324	                                         # signal trap (Ctrl+C safe)
325	   ```
326	
327	2. **Render** it conditionally in `window-status-format` so windows
328	   without the option set don't render anything extra. This repo's
329	   catppuccin theme already appends one such conditional in
330	   [`dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf`](../../dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf):
331	   ```tmux
332	   set -g @catppuccin_window_text ' #W#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}'
333	   ```
334	   To add YOUR badge, append another conditional:
335	   ```tmux
336	   set -g @catppuccin_window_text ' #W#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}#{?@my_status, #{@my_status},}'
337	   ```
338	   Both will coexist (workmux's 🤖 + your 🔨 next to each other when both
339	   are set on the same window).
340	
341	3. **Read** it back to verify or to gate logic:
342	   ```bash
343	   tmux show-options -wv -t 'mysession:3' '@my_status'
344	   tmux list-windows -aF '#{session_name}:#{window_index} marker=#{@my_status}'
345	   ```
346	
347	### When to invent your own user-var vs reuse `@workmux_status`
348	
349	Reuse `@workmux_status` if your status is conceptually "agent-like"
350	(working / waiting / done) — that way `wm sidebar` / `wm dashboard` /
351	`wm last-done` see your producer too, and `wmclear` resets it. Just call
352	`workmux set-window-status working` (or `waiting` / `done` / `clear`)
353	from your hook instead of writing the user-var directly.
354	
355	Invent a new `@<something>_status` user-var when:
356	- The state space differs (e.g. a build watcher with `building` /
357	  `passing` / `failing` is not workmux's working/waiting/done).
358	- You don't want it to appear in `wm dashboard` (workmux only knows
359	  about `@workmux_status`).
360	- Multiple producers should be visible simultaneously (workmux's icon
361	  and your build icon side by side).
362	
363	### Worked example: build watcher
364	
365	The simplest case — wrap any command and get start/success/failure
366	badges with one line, courtesy of `tmux_status_run`:
367	
368	```bash
369	tmux_status_run my_build 🔨 ✅ ❌ -- npm run build
370	```
371	
372	This sets `@my_build_status = 🔨` before the command, swaps to ✅ on
373	exit code 0 or ❌ on non-zero, and traps Ctrl+C / SIGTERM so the badge
374	clears instead of leaking. Wire it into a tmuxinator pre-command, a git
375	hook, a Makefile target, anywhere.
376	
377	For more nuanced lifecycles (multiple intermediate states like
378	`compiling` / `tests` / `bundling`), drop down to the raw helpers and
379	add the conditionals manually. Stream-parsing example:
380	
381	```bash
382	# ~/.local/bin/dev-watch.sh
383	. ~/.config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh
384	trap 'tmux_status_clear my_dev' EXIT INT TERM
385	npm run dev 2>&1 | while IFS= read -r line; do
386	  printf '%s\n' "$line"
387	  case "$line" in
388	    *"compiled successfully"*) tmux_status_set my_dev ✅ ;;
389	    *"failed to compile"*|*"error"*) tmux_status_set my_dev ❌ ;;
390	    *"compiling"*) tmux_status_set my_dev 🔨 ;;
391	  esac
392	done
393	```
394	
395	For BOTH approaches you must register the producer in the catppuccin
396	format ONCE (no wildcard support in tmux's `#{?...}` syntax). Append
397	your conditional to
398	[`dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf`](../../dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf)
399	alongside the workmux one:
400	
401	```tmux
402	set -g @catppuccin_window_text ' #W#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}#{?@my_dev_status, #{@my_dev_status},}'
403	```
404	
405	`tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf` (or new tmux session) and your window
406	shows `dev 🔨` while building, `dev ✅` when green, `dev ❌` on failure,
407	nothing when the script isn't running.
408	
409	### Shell helpers: `tmux_status_*`
410	
411	[`dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh`](../../dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh)
412	ships POSIX functions sourced by both zsh and bash (no zsh-only syntax,
413	safe to call from `#!/bin/sh` scripts too). All take a logical `name`
414	argument (no `@` prefix, no `_status` suffix — the helpers add them) so
415	the resulting tmux user-var is `@<name>_status`.
416	
417	| Function | Purpose |
418	|---|---|
419	| `tmux_status_set <name> <glyph> [target]` | Set marker on current window or `session:window` target |
420	| `tmux_status_get <name> [target]` | Read marker (empty + nonzero exit if unset) |
421	| `tmux_status_clear <name> [target]` | Unset marker on one window |
422	| `tmux_status_clear_all <name>` | Walk every window in every session, unset |
423	| `tmux_status_list` | Audit: print every `@*_status` user-var across all windows |
424	| `tmux_status_run <name> <working> <ok> <fail> -- <cmd>` | Wrap a command with badge transitions, trap-safe on Ctrl+C |
425	
426	Validation guards:
427	
428	- Empty / non-`[A-Za-z0-9_-]+` names → rejected with stderr diagnostic.
429	- Names starting with `workmux*` → rejected (reserved for the agent
430	  path; use `workmux set-window-status` for that).
431	- File silently no-ops the entire module when `tmux` isn't on PATH (cron,
432	  headless SSH, fresh box pre-ansible) — producers can call them
433	  unconditionally.
434	
435	### Lifecycle hard rules (learned the hard way)
436	
437	These mirror the workmux-leak debugging in
438	[`pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md`](../../pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md):
439	
440	- **Always have an unset path.** Set without unset = stuck marker
441	  forever. Use a `trap … EXIT INT TERM` if your producer is a script;
442	  use a `Stop` / `idle` event handler if your producer is an agent.
443	- **Sticky states need an explicit clearer.** `working`-style states
444	  (no auto-clear) need a counterpart event that calls unset. Workmux's
445	  bug was Anthropic shipping `set working` hooks without `set done` on
446	  Claude Stop — same trap awaits any custom integration.
447	- **Guard the producer with a `command -v` check** if it might run on a
448	  machine that doesn't have tmux loaded (cron, CI, SSH headless), so
449	  `tmux set-option` doesn't error and trash your hook log.
450	- **Pick a unique `@` prefix.** `@workmux_status` is taken; collisions
451	  silently wreck both producers. Convention: `@<tool>_status` or
452	  `@<your-username>_<purpose>`.
453	- **Per-window scope, not per-pane.** `tmux set-option -w` is window-
454	  level, so all panes in a window share the marker. If you need
455	  per-pane, use `set-option -p` and switch the format to use
456	  `#{?#{p:@my_status}, …}` — but the icon shows on the WINDOW tab, so
457	  per-window is almost always what you want.
458	
459	For the "see all markers across all sessions" debugging recipe, see
460	[`pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md`](../../pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md)
461	→ "Debugging recipe".

```text
1	# Workmux 🤖 status icon stuck on tmux window after agent exits
2	
3	## Symptoms
4	
5	- Tmux window list shows `1 zsh 🤖` after the OpenCode/Claude session
6	  in that window has been closed (Ctrl+C, kill pane, terminal crash).
7	- `tmux list-windows` shows `pane_current_command` is back to `zsh` /
8	  `bash`, but the 🤖 emoji persists in the window-status.
9	- Other windows that currently run an agent show no marker at all,
10	  while old "ghost" windows do.
11	- `tmux show -gv window-status-format` does NOT contain any emoji literal
12	  — searching `~/.tmux/`, `~/.config/tmux/`, all loaded plugins for
13	  `🤖|💬|✅` returns zero matches.
14	- `grep -rln '🤖' ~/.config ~/.local` finds nothing tmux-related.
15	- The marker only appears on SOME machines — fresh boxes never have it;
16	  only machines where you previously ran `workmux setup` (or `wm setup`).
17	
18	## Root cause
19	
20	The 🤖/💬/✅ icons come from [workmux](https://github.com/raine/workmux)
21	(`workmux` / `wm`), a tmux + git-worktree orchestrator. The mechanism is
22	**per-window tmux user options**:
23	
24	```
25	tmux set-option -w -t <session>:<window> @workmux_status '🤖'
26	```
27	
28	This was invisible to a normal grep-the-config search because:
29	
30	1. `@workmux_status` is a **per-window** option, not global. `tmux show -gv`
31	   only inspects global options. To see it: `tmux show-options -wA -t <window>`.
32	2. The `window-status-format` mod that `wm setup` does is **per-tmux-session**,
33	   set the first time `wm` runs in that session. It's not in any config
34	   file — only in tmux's runtime state.
35	3. The literal emoji never appears in any config file because the
36	   user-var value is set imperatively by `workmux set-window-status` from
37	   agent hooks at runtime.
38	
39	## Why the marker leaks
40	
41	Two distinct leak modes, both upstream design choices:
42	
43	### 1. `working` (🤖) is sticky by design
44	
45	From `workmux set-window-status --help`:
46	
47	| state | auto-clear |
48	|---|---|
49	| `working` | NEVER auto-clears |
50	| `waiting` | Auto-clears on window focus |
51	| `done` | Auto-clears on window focus |
52	
53	`working` only goes away when something explicitly calls
54	`workmux set-window-status done` (or `clear`). If the agent process dies
55	ungracefully (Ctrl+C, terminal crash, OOM, SSH disconnect), no `done`
56	event fires and the 🤖 sticks forever.
57	
58	### 2. Claude integration is set-only by upstream design
59	
60	Upstream `wm setup` writes `~/.claude/settings.json` hooks that only
61	**set** `working` on `PostToolUse` / `UserPromptSubmit`. There is **no
62	`Stop` hook calling `set-window-status done`** in the upstream install.
63	Every Claude turn ends with 🤖 still showing — even on graceful exit.
64	
65	OpenCode is better: its plugin listens for `session.idle` and calls
66	`done`. That fixes the graceful-shutdown case but not the crash case.
67	
68	## Fix
69	
70	This repo ships three layers of mitigation, all chezmoi-managed so they
71	auto-deploy on every box. See [docs/tools/workmux.md](../docs/tools/workmux.md)
72	for the full integration story; in pitfall-form:
73	
74	1. **Claude `Stop` + `SubagentStop` hooks** —
75	   [`dot_claude/modify_settings.json`](../dot_claude/modify_settings.json)
76	   adds explicit `workmux set-window-status done` calls on every turn end.
77	   Fixes the by-design Claude leak. The hook-aware merger preserves any
78	   parallel entries from CodeIsland or `wm setup`.
79	
80	2. **OpenCode `session.idle` plugin** —
81	   [`dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts`](../dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts)
82	   vendored from upstream. Handles graceful-shutdown leak.
83	
84	3. **Self-managed window-status-format** —
85	   [`dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf`](../dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf)
86	   appends `#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}` to catppuccin's
87	   window text overrides. Plus `status_format: false` in
88	   [`dot_config/workmux/config.yaml`](../dot_config/workmux/config.yaml)
89	   tells `wm` not to also do its own per-session rewrite. Result: icons
90	   render in every tmux session consistently, survive `chezmoi diff`,
91	   don't fight catppuccin.
92	
93	For the residual crash-leak case (any agent killed without firing its
94	hook): use `wmclear` from
95	[`dot_config/zsh/tools/38_workmux.zsh`](../dot_config/zsh/tools/38_workmux.zsh),
96	or run `wm sidebar` (auto-detects 10s pane silence and downgrades stuck
97	`working`).
98	
99	## Debugging recipe (next time the marker behaves weirdly)
100	
101	```bash
102	# 1. Is workmux even installed on this machine?
103	command -v workmux && workmux --version
104	
105	# 2. What's the per-window state?
106	tmux list-windows -aF '#{session_name}:#{window_index} name=#{window_name} marker=#{@workmux_status}'
107	
108	# 3. What's the per-session window-status-format?
109	#    (workmux self-manages this if status_format:true; we set it to false)
110	tmux show -gv window-status-format
111	tmux show -gv @catppuccin_window_text  # our self-managed path
112	
113	# 4. Where are the agent hooks actually pointing?
114	jq '.hooks' ~/.claude/settings.json
115	ls ~/.config/opencode/plugins/
116	
117	# 5. Manual escape hatch when stuck
118	wmclear           # current window
119	wmclear --all     # entire current session
120	```
121	
122	## Related
123	
124	- [docs/tools/workmux.md](../docs/tools/workmux.md) — integration overview.
125	- [docs/tools/agent-overlays.md](../docs/tools/agent-overlays.md) — the
126	  hook-aware merger pattern in `modify_settings.json`.
127	- [backlog/tmux-window-status-indicators.md](../backlog/tmux-window-status-indicators.md)
128	  — original design exploration that predicted exactly this lifecycle bug
129	  before workmux was discovered as the upstream solution. Closed by this
130	  pitfall.
131
```

```text
1	// ~/.config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts
2	// Source: dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts (managed by chezmoi)
3	//
4	// Mirrors the upstream plugin from raine/workmux:
5	//   https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raine/workmux/main/resources/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts
6	//
7	// Why managed here: workmux's `wm setup` writes this file on first run, but
8	// only on machines where you remembered to run setup. Tracking it in chezmoi
9	// makes the integration auto-deploy on every fresh box.
10	//
11	// Refresh strategy: `wm` itself is install-only via ansible (see
12	// dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml) — we don't auto-bump it. When
13	// you `just upgrade-tools` and workmux ships a new plugin schema, copy the
14	// upstream file over this one:
15	//   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raine/workmux/main/resources/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts \
16	//     > $(chezmoi source-path ~/.config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts)
17	//
18	// Companion package.json lives next to this file (also chezmoi-managed) so
19	// OpenCode resolves @opencode-ai/plugin without us shipping node_modules.
20	//
21	// Status semantics (from `workmux set-window-status --help`):
22	//   working — agent processing                (sticky; never auto-clears)
23	//   waiting — agent needs user input          (auto-clears on window focus)
24	//   done    — agent finished                  (auto-clears on window focus)
25	// See docs/tools/workmux.md for the lifecycle / leak story.
26	
27	import type { Plugin } from '@opencode-ai/plugin';
28	
29	export const WorkmuxStatusPlugin: Plugin = async ({ $ }) => {
30	  // OpenCode can emit repeated `session.status busy` events for a single turn,
31	  // and can even emit a stale trailing `busy` after `idle` at the end. Track
32	  // per-session status so workmux only sees real transitions.
33	  const lastStatusBySession = new Map<string, string>();
34	  const acceptBusyBySession = new Map<string, boolean>();
35	
36	  async function setStatus(
37	    sessionID: string | undefined,
38	    status: string,
39	  ) {
40	    if (!sessionID) {
41	      return;
42	    }
43	
44	    const previous = lastStatusBySession.get(sessionID);
45	    // Ignore the final stale `busy` OpenCode sometimes emits after a session is
46	    // already done. The next user message re-arms `working` for the new turn.
47	    if (status === 'working' && acceptBusyBySession.get(sessionID) === false) {
48	      return;
49	    }
50	    if (previous === status) {
51	      return;
52	    }
53	
54	    lastStatusBySession.set(sessionID, status);
55	    if (status === 'done') {
56	      acceptBusyBySession.set(sessionID, false);
57	    } else {
58	      acceptBusyBySession.set(sessionID, true);
59	    }
60	
61	    await $`workmux set-window-status ${status}`.quiet();
62	  }
63	
64	  return {
65	    event: async ({ event }) => {
66	      if (event.type === 'message.updated' && event.properties.info.role === 'user') {
67	        acceptBusyBySession.set(event.properties.sessionID, true);
68	      }
69	
70	      switch (event.type) {
71	        case 'session.status':
72	          if (event.properties.status.type === 'busy') {
73	            await setStatus(event.properties.sessionID, 'working');
74	          }
75	          if (event.properties.status.type === 'idle') {
76	            await setStatus(event.properties.sessionID, 'done');
77	          }
78	          break;
79	        case 'permission.asked':
80	        case 'question.asked':
81	          await setStatus(event.properties.sessionID, 'waiting');
82	          break;
83	        case 'permission.replied':
84	        case 'question.replied':
85	          await setStatus(event.properties.sessionID, 'working');
86	          break;
87	        case 'session.idle':
88	          await setStatus(event.properties.sessionID, 'done');
89	          break;
90	      }
91	    },
92	  };
93	};
94
```

# Dotfiles Repository — Agent Contract

Cross-platform dotfiles managed by **chezmoi** (configs) + **ansible** (system deps). This file is the agent-facing contract: edit rules and cross-file invariants. User-facing intro: [README.md](README.md).

> **Headroom rule**: keep this file under ~30k chars. Push handbook content into `docs/`; keep only rules an agent must obey *without* opening another file. `AGENTS.md` and `GEMINI.md` are symlinks to this file — edit one.

## Cross-file maintenance rules

When you touch one of these surfaces, update the listed mirror in the same commit.

| Surface you change | Also update | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| Config files / ansible roles / platforms / setup steps | `README.md` (What You Get, Supported Platforms, Quick Setup) | — |
| New `docs/**/*.md` | Nav entry in `mkdocs.yml`; run `uv run mkdocs build --strict` | known anchor-drift is tracked in [`backlog/mkdocs-anchor-drift.md`](backlog/mkdocs-anchor-drift.md) — don't tighten `validation.links.not_found` until cleared |
| Alias / shell function in `dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/` | Row in [docs/shells/aliases.md](docs/shells/aliases.md) (name, type, source, scope, one-line) | [docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md](docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md) for repo-wide config conventions |
| Shell history env vars / `setopt`s / atuin filters | Tables in [docs/shells/history.md](docs/shells/history.md) | — |
| Linux GUI app in `dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/` | Inventory table in [docs/playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md](docs/playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md) (the playbook is also the decision tree — read first) | — |
| New `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` prompt | `Dockerfile` ARG + `chezmoi init` flag, `PROMPTS` tuple in `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py` (+ `BUNDLES` if applicable); verify with `uv run --script scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py doctor` | — |
| `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_fleet` (umbrella `fleet chezmoi <action>` namespace + top-level generic primitives `tmux`/`info`/`pueue`/`exec`/`hosts`/`edit`) / `scripts/fleet/` (`apply.py` / `tmux.py` / `info.py` / `pueue.py` / `exec.py` / `hosts.py`) / `justfile` `fleet` + `fleet-*` recipes / `dot_config/fleet/` / `dot_config/television/cable/fleet-hosts.toml` / sudo helper consumption / `dot_config/tmux/executable_tmux-session-summary.py` `--json` schema / `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_pqsum` `json`/`ai --stdin-json` schemas / `scripts/fleet/exec.py` PATH-prelude + AIEXEC schema | [docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md), [docs/tools/pueue.md](docs/tools/pueue.md), [docs/tools/fleet-exec.md](docs/tools/fleet-exec.md), [docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md](docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md) | The `--json` schema emitted by `tmux-session-summary.py` and the raw-fallback parser in `scripts/fleet/tmux.py:_parse_raw` MUST stay in sync — adding a field to `Session`/`Window` dataclass means updating both. Same rule for `executable_pqsum`'s `HostSnapshot`/`GroupRec`/`TaskRec` dataclasses ↔ `scripts/fleet/pueue.py` `_run_pqsum_ai` payload — fleet pipes raw `pueue status --json` through `pqsum json --raw-stdin --host=NAME` and feeds the result to `pqsum ai --stdin-json --multi-host`, so any change to pqsum's output keys breaks fleet's AI mode silently. The PATH-augmentation prelude in `scripts/fleet/pueue.py:_REMOTE_CMD` and `scripts/fleet/exec.py:_PATH_PRELUDE` MUST stay in sync — both rely on the same chezmoi → cargo → uv → ~/bin → brew → linuxbrew order (deliberately diverges from the user's interactive shell PATH so package-manager dirs win over legacy ~/bin). |
| `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_mlf` / `scripts/mlf/{tui,plot,list,download}.py` / `dot_config/television/cable/mlflow.toml` keybindings | Mirror single-letter mnemonics across the two UIs: the TUI `BINDINGS` letters (`b`/`y`/`p`/`d`/`j`) and the tv channel's `Ctrl+<letter>` actions are intentionally the same so muscle memory carries across `mlf` (dashboard) ↔ `tv mlflow` (picker). Change one → change the other in the same commit. | Shared helpers (`open_id`/`copy_id`/`fetch_histories`/`detect_kind`/`make_client`) live in `scripts/mlf/__init__.py` — refactor there, not in the call sites. The two UIs coexist intentionally: tv = fast picker, mlf TUI = multi-pane dashboard. |
| New coding-agent artifact dir with secret risk | `DEFAULT_PATHS` in `scripts/redact_secrets.py` + `files:` regex in `redact-agent-secrets` pre-commit hook | Currently auto-scanned: `.specstory/history/`, `.claude/plans/`, `.cursor/plans/`, `.opencode/plans/` |
| Keybinding (`Ctrl+`/`Alt+`) in any tool config | Cross-check namespace before claiming — tmux root-table `bind -n C-*` shadows inner apps; prefer `Alt+` for new actions | [docs/shells/keybindings.md](docs/shells/keybindings.md), [docs/tools/claude-code-keybindings.md](docs/tools/claude-code-keybindings.md), [docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md](docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md) |
| AI agent autodetect order or `AICAP_*_MODEL` defaults | Edit **only** [`dot_config/shell/04_ai_agents.sh`](dot_config/shell/04_ai_agents.sh) — the SSOT. Both shells source it; the **four** Python consumers (`dot_config/tmux/executable_tmux-session-summary.py`, `scripts/aiblock.py`, `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_pqsum`, `scripts/fleet/exec.py`) regex-parse the same file for cron / tmux-popup contexts where env isn't inherited. Each agent's `-m`/`--model` flag is conditional on its env var being non-empty so a retired model ID falls through to the CLI's own default. When adding a NEW agent, update: SSOT (one new `AICAP_<AGENT>_MODEL` line), `04_ai_capture.sh:_aiagent_invoke` case, **all four** Python `AGENT_CONFIG` dicts. **Four consumers = pain threshold reached** — the extraction TODO (`scripts/aisum/__init__.py`) is now blocking ergonomics; next AI-tooling change should land that refactor before adding more callsites. | — |
| chezmoi-apply reload hint: `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_after_99_signal_reload.sh.tmpl` (touches sentinel) ↔ `dot_config/shell/99_chezmoi_reload.sh` (reads sentinel + zsh/bash hook registration + `cas`/`cau` wrappers) | Row in [docs/shells/aliases.md](docs/shells/aliases.md) "Dotfiles management" section for `cas`/`cau` | The sentinel path `~/.cache/chezmoi/last-apply` is hard-coded in **two** places — the run-script that touches it and the shared backend that reads it. Keep both in sync when relocating (e.g. switching to `$XDG_STATE_HOME`). Hook registration is in the shared backend (NOT `dot_config/{zsh,bash}/99_*`) because bash's `$BASH_CONFIG_DIR` loads before `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/shell` (oh-my-bash `plugins=()` prereq, see `dot_bashrc.tmpl:94` vs `:114`), so a per-shell hook file in `dot_config/bash/` would run before the backend function exists. Opt out: `export CHEZMOI_RELOAD_HINT=0`. |

**Repo-root files that stay OUT of MkDocs nav** (`README.md`, `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` / `GEMINI.md`, `TODO.md`, `backlog/`, `pitfalls/`, `NOTES.md`): referenced via absolute GitHub URLs from [`docs/for-maintainers.md`](docs/for-maintainers.md), never copied via `pymdownx.snippets`.

**Three-tier file placement** for new shell helpers:

| Tier | Dir | When |
|---|---|---|
| Shared | `dot_config/shell/` | POSIX subset, both shells source. `$ZSH_VERSION`/`$BASH_VERSION` source-time dispatch is OK; ZLE widgets / `compdef` / `bindkey` / `setopt` / `read -q` / `${m:t}` / glob qualifiers are NOT (bash would error on source). |
| Zsh-only | `dot_config/zsh/` | ZLE widgets, `compdef`, `bindkey`, `setopt`, zsh-vi-mode hooks. |
| Bash-only | `dot_config/bash/` | `bind -x` / `ble-bind`, OMB plugin arrays, bash-specific `shopt`s. |

When porting a zsh-only helper to bash via ble.sh, extract the shell-agnostic backend into `dot_config/shell/` and keep each shell's widget binding in its own dir.

### Workmux status icon integration spans 6 files

Touching the `🤖`/`💬`/`✅` per-tmux-window status mechanism requires keeping these 6 surfaces in sync (full story: [docs/tools/workmux.md](docs/tools/workmux.md); pitfall: [pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md](pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md)):

1. `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` — binary install (brew tap on macOS; GitHub release `.tar.gz` on Linux)
2. `dot_config/workmux/config.yaml` — `status_format: false` is load-bearing
3. `dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf` — `#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}` appended to `@catppuccin_window_text` and `@catppuccin_window_current_text`
4. `dot_claude/modify_settings.json` — `Stop`/`SubagentStop`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`Notification` hooks calling `workmux set-window-status` (hook-aware merger preserves CodeIsland entries)
5. `dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts` + `dot_config/opencode/modify_package.json`
6. `dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh` — generic POSIX `tmux_status_set/get/clear/clear_all/list/run` for non-agent producers

**Hard rules**: never run `workmux setup` on a managed machine (would write parallel hook entries); never flip `status_format: true` (fights catppuccin's window-text override); never drop the `command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && … || true` guard in Claude hooks (spams errors on fresh boxes); never drop explicit `set-window-status done` from `Stop`/`SubagentStop` (upstream only ever sets `working`, never clears — that's the by-design leak documented in the pitfall). `wt` (worktrunk, `37_worktrunk.zsh`) and `wm` (workmux, `38_workmux.zsh`) stay distinct — different config formats, killer features, helper files.

### Long-term backlog + past pitfalls → use the `project-knowledge-harness` skill

This repo uses the `project-knowledge-harness` agent skill (restored on every `chezmoi apply` via `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl`; see [docs/tools/agent-skills.md](docs/tools/agent-skills.md)). **Load the skill** for the template, disambiguation table, and upgrade path.

**Fallback rules** so this section still binds when the skill cannot be loaded:

- Three repo-root surfaces, all chezmoi-ignored, all NOT auto-redacted: [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) (priority/effort tags `P1`/`P2`/`P3`/`P?` × `S`/`M`/`L`/`XL`), [`backlog/`](backlog/README.md) (research/design notes for `P?` / `[L]` / `[XL]` / multi-option), [`pitfalls/`](pitfalls/README.md) (debugged traps — **title by symptom, not root cause**, verbatim error messages, never paraphrase).
- Capture triggers — future work: "maybe later", "nice to have", "工程量太大需要再評估", "先記下來". Pitfalls: >~15 min debugging, not googleable, non-obvious fix, silent failure.
- Do **not** spawn `ROADMAP.md` / `IDEAS.md` / `LESSONS.md` / `TROUBLESHOOTING.md`. Three surfaces, always.
- A pitfall *graduates* to a Hard invariant below when it (a) recurs across machines, (b) silently corrupts state, or (c) has a non-obvious workaround. Link back to `pitfalls/<slug>.md`.

## Chezmoi templating conventions

**Hard rule**: before adding `{{ if eq .profile … }}`, ask if the predicate is auto-detectable. If yes, use `.chezmoi.os` / `.chezmoi.arch` / `.chezmoi.hostname`. `.profile` is for user-role choices only. Values are limited to `macos`, `ubuntu_desktop`, `ubuntu_server` — do **not** introduce new values for OS/arch facts (historical `macos_intel` profile was removed for exactly this reason).

| Predicate | Use |
|---|---|
| Any macOS | `eq .chezmoi.os "darwin"` |
| Any Linux | `eq .chezmoi.os "linux"` |
| Apple Silicon | `eq .chezmoi.arch "arm64"` (in darwin scope) or `and (eq .chezmoi.os "darwin") (eq .chezmoi.arch "arm64")` |
| Intel Mac | `and (eq .chezmoi.os "darwin") (eq .chezmoi.arch "amd64")` |
| Desktop vs headless | `.profile` — `ubuntu_desktop` / `ubuntu_server` |

Decision table, before/after examples, `macos_intel` migration: [docs/tools/chezmoi-templating.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-templating.md).

## Hard repo invariants

### Validate app configs with the app, not just syntax

Template rendering / YAML / TOML / JSON syntax is not enough. If the app exposes a config check, parser, dry-run, or debug command, run it against the rendered config before declaring done (e.g. `codex debug …` for `~/.codex/config.toml`; `tmux source-file` / `display-menu` smoke for tmux; `mkdocs build --strict` for docs; for Ansible run the narrowest practical play/tag/check-mode or container smoke — `--syntax-check` alone is a first pass). If a validator cannot be run, say so explicitly in the final report and name the missing command/host/credential.

### `primaryShell` choice gates `chsh` only — both shells always deploy

`primaryShell` (`zsh` | `bash`, default `zsh`) **only** governs which login shell `chsh` switches to. Both `~/.zshrc`, `~/.bashrc`, `~/.config/{shell,zsh,bash}/` deploy everywhere — users routinely drop into the other shell ad-hoc.

**Hard rules**:

- Do **not** add `{{ if eq .primaryShell … }}` gates around `dot_zshrc.tmpl`, `dot_bashrc.tmpl`, or `dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/**`.
- Do **not** gate the zsh / bash ansible roles' **package install** task on `primary_shell` — only `chsh` is gated. macOS bash 5.x brew install + `/etc/shells` whitelist are gated on `primary_shell == "bash"` (zsh-primary mac users skip the brew formula).
- Do **not** rely on `$SHELL` — it reflects `/etc/passwd`, lags `chsh` until next login. Use `$ZSH_VERSION` / `$BASH_VERSION`.

ble.sh + oh-my-bash 12-step init order in `dot_bashrc.tmpl` is load-bearing: `ble.sh --attach=none` MUST source before bash-preexec/starship; `ble-attach` MUST be the last call before secrets/adhoc; OMB's `autosuggestions` / `syntax-highlighting` / `history-substring-search` plugins MUST be excluded (ble.sh provides natives; double-init causes flicker). Full breakdown: [docs/shells/bash.md](docs/shells/bash.md).

### Three-tier user-local override layer

User overrides live in **six** untracked files: shared POSIX (`~/.shellrc.adhoc`, `~/.shellrc.secrets`) and per-shell (`~/.zshrc.adhoc`, `~/.bashrc.adhoc`, `~/.config/zsh/secrets.zsh`, `~/.config/bash/secrets.sh`). All six in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`. Default target: shared. Drop to per-shell only when shell-specific syntax is required.

305	  choose-tree -Zs -F "#{session_name}" \

308	  display-message "Pick destination session to BREAK pane into (as new window)…" \; \

310	  "run-shell '~/.config/tmux/cross-session.sh break %%'"
311	bind A run-shell "tmux set-environment -g _src_window '#{window_id}'" \; \
312	  display-message "Pick destination session to LINK window into (window lives in both)…" \; \
313	  choose-tree -Zs -F "#{session_name}" \
314	  "run-shell '~/.config/tmux/cross-session.sh link %%'"
