316	# prefix + E : explode — break EVERY pane in current window into its own window
317	#              within the SAME session. Use case: switching from wide screen
318	#              (multi-pane layout) to mobile/SSH where one pane per window is
319	#              easier than zooming with prefix + z. Source window keeps the
320	#              first pane; other panes become sibling windows inserted right
321	#              after it, named after each pane's current command.

324	# =============================================================================
325	# Theme Switching (Catppuccin <-> tmux2k)

330	  tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf; \
331	  tmux display-message 'Theme: catppuccin'"
332	
333	bind M-t run-shell "tmux set -g @theme_variant tmux2k; \
334	  tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf; \
335	  tmux display-message 'Theme: tmux2k'"
336	
337	# =============================================================================
338	# Sesh (tmux session manager)
339	# =============================================================================
340	
341	# prefix + g: sesh picker in a tmux popup with fzf
342	bind-key "g" run-shell "sesh connect \"$(\
343	  sesh list --icons | fzf-tmux -p 80%,70% \
344	    --no-sort --ansi --border-label ' sesh ' --prompt '⚡  ' \
345	    --header '  ^a all ^t tmux ^g configs ^x zoxide ^d tmux kill ^f find' \
346	    --bind 'tab:down,btab:up' \
347	    --bind 'ctrl-a:change-prompt(⚡  )+reload(sesh list --icons)' \
348	    --bind 'ctrl-t:change-prompt(🪟  )+reload(sesh list -t --icons)' \
349	    --bind 'ctrl-g:change-prompt(⚙️  )+reload(sesh list -c --icons)' \
350	    --bind 'ctrl-x:change-prompt(📁  )+reload(sesh list -z --icons)' \
351	    --bind 'ctrl-f:change-prompt(🔎  )+reload(fd -H -d 2 -t d -E .Trash . ~)' \
352	    --bind 'ctrl-d:execute(tmux kill-session -t {2..})+change-prompt(⚡  )+reload(sesh list --icons)' \
353	    --preview-window 'right:55%' \
354	    --preview 'sesh preview {}' \
355	)\""
356	
357	bind -N "last-session (via sesh)" S run-shell "sesh last 2>/dev/null || tmux display-message 'No previous sesh session'"
358	
359	# prefix + 9: open repo-aware coding-agent layout (`scode`) for the current
360	# pane's directory. scode walks up from cwd to find .git; if not in a repo,
361	# the error surfaces in the tmux status line.
362	# Replaces the previous `sesh connect --root $(pwd)` binding (which had a
363	# subtle bug — $(pwd) was expanded once at config parse time, not per-press).
364	# Logic is in scode-here.sh because tmux run-shell is /bin/sh (can't see
365	# zsh functions) and the session-name + switch-client dance is non-trivial.
366	bind -N "scode for current dir (repo-aware coding layout)" 9 \
367	  run-shell -b "~/.config/tmux/scode-here.sh '#{pane_current_path}'"
368	
369	# prefix + 0: lightweight counterpart to prefix+9. Plain sesh session at
370	# the git root of the current pane's directory (no nvim/agent layout).
371	# Replaces tmux's built-in `select-window -t :=0` which always errored
372	# because base-index is 1 (no window 0 exists). Logic in sesh-root-here.sh
373	# — see that file for the two bugs in the original `sesh connect --root
374	# $(pwd)` binding (parse-time $(pwd) + misuse of --root flag).
375	bind -N "sesh-root for current dir (lightweight)" 0 \
376	  run-shell -b "~/.config/tmux/sesh-root-here.sh '#{pane_current_path}'"
377	
378	# prefix + T: sesh picker via television (tv) in a tmux popup
379	bind-key "T" display-popup -E -w 80% -h 70% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' Sesh (tv) ' "tv sesh"
380	
381	# prefix + O: sesh built-in picker in a tmux popup
382	bind-key "O" display-popup -h 90% -w 50% -E "sesh picker -i"
383	
384	# prefix + U: CLI tools picker via television (tv tools)
385	bind-key "U" display-popup -E -w 80% -h 70% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' CLI Tools (tv) ' "tv tools"
386	
387	# prefix + a: live coding-agent panes picker (tv agent-panes)
388	# Shows claude / cursor-agent / codex / opencode sessions currently running in
389	# any tmux pane. Enter switches focus to that pane. See:
390	#   docs/tools/agent-panes-discovery.md
391	bind-key "a" display-popup -E -w 80% -h 70% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' Live agent panes (tv) ' "tv agent-panes"
392	
393	# (prefix + W is now bound earlier in this file as `kill-window`. The previous
394	# `sesh window` binding was removed because `sesh` has no `window` subcommand;
395	# pressing it printed sesh's help to a popup. See git history.)
396	
397	# =============================================================================
398	# Popup tools (display-popup -E -d '#{pane_current_path}')
399	# =============================================================================
400	# Floating scratch pane (tmux-floax) is on prefix + F (toggleable, persistent
401	# session named `float`). The bindings below are one-shot popups that close
402	# when the inner command exits — handy for "do one thing without disrupting
403	# the layout" workflows.
404	
405	# prefix + G: lazygit popup at current pane path
406	bind-key "G" display-popup -E -w 90% -h 90% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' lazygit ' "lazygit"
407	
408	# prefix + ` (backtick): one-shot popup shell at current pane path.
409	# Closes when the inner shell exits (`exit` or Ctrl-D). Each invocation gets
410	# a fresh shell — no state preserved. For a persistent scratchpad with
411	# history, use floax (prefix + F) instead.
412	bind-key '`' display-popup -E -w 80% -h 80% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' shell '
413	
414	# =============================================================================
415	# Help / cheatsheet
416	# =============================================================================
417	# tmux's built-in `prefix + ?` (list-keys -N) is hard to scan and can't search
418	# user-defined bindings well. We replace it with tmux-fzf's keybinding picker
419	# (fzf popup, fuzzy-searchable). The original list-keys is still reachable on
420	# `prefix + C-?` as a fallback.
421	#
422	# `prefix + /` (built-in: prompt for a key, show what it's bound to) is left
423	# alone — it's already useful for "what does THIS key do?" lookups.
424	#
425	# `?` inside the prefix + Enter popup menu opens a glow-rendered
426	# cheatsheet (curated, grouped, prettier than list-keys).
427	
428	unbind-key '?'
429	bind-key '?' run-shell -b "~/.tmux/plugins/tmux-fzf/main.sh"
430	bind-key 'C-?' list-keys -N
431	
432	# `/` inside the Enter-popup uses this; standalone prefix + / stays built-in
433	# (key-prompt). We expose the cheatsheet through the popup menu's `?` entry.
434	bind-key M-/ display-popup -E -w 80% -h 80% -T ' tmux cheatsheet ' \
435	  "glow -p ~/.config/tmux/cheatsheet.md 2>/dev/null \
436	    || less ~/.config/tmux/cheatsheet.md"
437	
438	# =============================================================================
439	# Popup Menu (prefix + Space)
440	# =============================================================================
441	# Two entry keys, same menu. The menu itself is generated by a script
442	# (`~/.config/tmux/menu.sh`) which:
443	#
444	#   1. Reads `#{client_height}` and emits a tier-trimmed row list. tmux's
445	#      `display-menu` does NOT paginate — if the menu is taller than the
446	#      terminal, the entire popup is silently suppressed (no error). The
447	#      script keeps the menu fitting on tiny mobile-SSH heights too.
448	#   2. Submenus are sibling scripts (menu-layouts.sh, menu-session.sh,
449	#      menu-sesh.sh, menu-popups.sh, menu-theme.sh, menu-system.sh). Each
450	#      `exec tmux display-menu …` so quoting context resets per submenu —
451	#      no nested-quote escaping disasters in keybindings.conf.
452	#
453	# History: an earlier flat ~50-row menu silently failed on smaller heights
454	# and was misdiagnosed as a csi-u key encoding bug, then as a quoting bug.
455	# Both real (the `\;` accelerator was broken, sesh fzf binds had nested-
456	# quote issues), but the dominant symptom — "menu doesn't open at all" —
457	# was actually menu-too-tall. See pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-parse-failure.md.
458	#
459	# Discovery fallbacks if you forget the keys: `prefix + ?` (tmux-fzf fuzzy
460	# picker over every binding), `prefix + M-/` (glow cheatsheet popup), or
461	# right-click on a pane / status line.
462	
463	unbind-key Space
464	unbind-key Enter
465	bind-key Space run-shell "~/.config/tmux/menu.sh"
466	# Note: `prefix + e` was previously a popup-menu alias (added as workaround
467	# for a misdiagnosed display-menu bug — see pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md).
468	# Removed so `e` is free as a sub-menu mnemonic (e.g. "Even layout: horizontal"
469	# in the window right-click menu).

1	# ~/.config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh
2	# Source: dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh (managed by chezmoi)
3	#
4	# Generic per-window tmux status badge helpers — POSIX, sourced by both
5	# zsh and bash. Thin convenience layer over the same primitive workmux
6	# uses (`tmux set-option -w '@<name>_status' '<glyph>'`), so any script /
7	# hook / cron job / build watcher can tag its tmux window without
8	# pulling in workmux.
9	#
10	# Why a shared layer (not in 38_workmux.zsh): these helpers don't need
11	# any zsh feature, and the most common consumers (build scripts, deploy
12	# hooks, CI wrappers) tend to be `#!/bin/bash` or `#!/bin/sh`. Putting
13	# them in dot_config/shell/ means they Just Work from any shell.
14	#
15	# Companion: docs/tools/workmux.md → "Reusing the per-window status
16	# mechanism (without workmux)" for design rationale, the lifecycle hard
17	# rules, and the build-watcher worked example.
18	#
19	# Quick reference:
20	#
21	#   tmux_status_set my_build 🔨           # tag current window
22	#   tmux_status_set my_build 🔨 mysess:3  # tag specific window
23	#   tmux_status_get my_build              # read current window
24	#   tmux_status_clear my_build            # unset (current window)
25	#   tmux_status_clear my_build mysess:3   # unset specific window
26	#   tmux_status_clear_all my_build        # unset across every session
27	#   tmux_status_list                      # list every @*_status user-var
28	#   tmux_status_run my_build 🔨 ✅ ❌ -- npm run build
29	#                                         # set 🔨, run cmd, set ✅/❌
30	#                                         # by exit code, auto-clear on
31	#                                         # signal trap
32	#
33	# Naming convention: pass the LOGICAL name without `@` or `_status`
34	# suffix — these helpers add the `@<name>_status` wrapper. So
35	# `tmux_status_set my_build 🔨` writes `@my_build_status`. This keeps
36	# the user-var namespace tidy (`@<tool>_status` everywhere) and lets
37	# you grep for "every status producer" with `tmux_status_list`.
38	
39	# Skip silently if tmux isn't on PATH (cron, headless SSH, fresh box
40	# pre-ansible). Producers can call these unconditionally.
41	command -v tmux >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
42	
43	# Internal: validate name (alphanumeric + underscore + dash, no `@` /
44	# `_status` since we add them). Returns 0 if valid, 1 if not (with
45	# stderr diagnostic). Empty name is rejected. Names starting with
46	# `workmux` are reserved to avoid clobbering workmux's own user-var.
47	_tmux_status_validate_name() {
48	    if [ -z "${1:-}" ]; then
49	        printf 'tmux_status: name argument is required\n' >&2
50	        return 1
51	    fi
52	    case "$1" in
53	        workmux*)
54	            # shellcheck disable=SC2016 # Backticks here are literal Markdown-style code spans, not command substitution.
55	            printf 'tmux_status: name "%s" reserved (workmux owns @workmux_status). Use `workmux set-window-status` for the agent path.\n' "$1" >&2
56	            return 1
57	            ;;
58	        *[!A-Za-z0-9_-]*)
59	            printf 'tmux_status: name "%s" must be [A-Za-z0-9_-]+\n' "$1" >&2
60	            return 1
61	            ;;
62	    esac
63	    return 0
64	}
65	
66	# tmux_status_set <name> <glyph> [target]
67	#   target defaults to current window (`tmux display -p '#{session_name}:#{window_index}'`)
68	tmux_status_set() {
69	    _tmux_status_validate_name "${1:-}" || return 1
70	    if [ $# -lt 2 ]; then
71	        printf 'tmux_status_set: usage: tmux_status_set <name> <glyph> [target]\n' >&2
72	        return 1
73	    fi
74	    _name="$1"
75	    _glyph="$2"
76	    _target="${3:-}"
77	    if [ -n "$_target" ]; then
78	        tmux set-option -w -t "$_target" "@${_name}_status" "$_glyph" 2>/dev/null
79	    else
80	        tmux set-option -w "@${_name}_status" "$_glyph" 2>/dev/null
81	    fi
82	}
83	
84	# tmux_status_get <name> [target]
85	#   prints the glyph (or empty string + non-zero exit if unset)
86	tmux_status_get() {
87	    _tmux_status_validate_name "${1:-}" || return 1
88	    _name="$1"
89	    _target="${2:-}"
90	    if [ -n "$_target" ]; then
91	        tmux show-options -wv -t "$_target" "@${_name}_status" 2>/dev/null
92	    else
93	        tmux show-options -wv "@${_name}_status" 2>/dev/null
94	    fi
95	}
96	
97	# tmux_status_clear <name> [target]
98	tmux_status_clear() {
99	    _tmux_status_validate_name "${1:-}" || return 1
100	    _name="$1"
101	    _target="${2:-}"
102	    if [ -n "$_target" ]; then
103	        tmux set-option -w -t "$_target" -u "@${_name}_status" 2>/dev/null
104	    else
105	        tmux set-option -w -u "@${_name}_status" 2>/dev/null
106	    fi
107	}
108	
109	# tmux_status_clear_all <name>
110	#   walk every window in every session, unset @<name>_status
111	tmux_status_clear_all() {
112	    _tmux_status_validate_name "${1:-}" || return 1
113	    _name="$1"
114	    tmux list-windows -aF '#{session_name}:#{window_index}' 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r _w; do
115	        tmux set-option -w -t "$_w" -u "@${_name}_status" 2>/dev/null
116	    done
117	}
118	
119	# tmux_status_list
120	#   show every @*_status user-var across every window (read-only audit)
121	tmux_status_list() {
122	    tmux list-windows -aF '#{session_name}:#{window_index} #{window_name}' 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r _line; do
123	        _w="${_line%% *}"
124	        # Pull every option starting with @ on this window, filter to *_status
125	        tmux show-options -w -t "$_w" 2>/dev/null \
126	            | awk -v w="$_line" '/^@[A-Za-z0-9_-]+_status / {print w "  " $0}'
127	    done
128	}
129	
130	# tmux_status_run <name> <working_glyph> <ok_glyph> <fail_glyph> -- <cmd> [args...]
131	#   Run a command, badge the window with `working_glyph` while it runs,
132	#   then `ok_glyph` on success or `fail_glyph` on failure. Traps INT /
133	#   TERM / HUP to clear the badge instead of leaking on Ctrl+C.
134	#
135	#   Example:
136	#     tmux_status_run my_build 🔨 ✅ ❌ -- npm run build
137	#     tmux_status_run deploy   🚀 🟢 🔴 -- ./deploy.sh prod
138	tmux_status_run() {
139	    _tmux_status_validate_name "${1:-}" || return 1
140	    if [ $# -lt 6 ]; then
141	        printf 'tmux_status_run: usage: tmux_status_run <name> <working> <ok> <fail> -- <cmd> [args...]\n' >&2
142	        return 1
143	    fi
144	    _name="$1"
145	    _working="$2"
146	    _ok="$3"
147	    _fail="$4"
148	    shift 4
149	    if [ "${1:-}" != "--" ]; then
150	        # shellcheck disable=SC2016 # Backticks are literal in the diagnostic message.
151	        printf 'tmux_status_run: missing `--` separator before command\n' >&2
152	        return 1
153	    fi
154	    shift
155	    if [ $# -eq 0 ]; then
156	        # shellcheck disable=SC2016 # Backticks are literal in the diagnostic message.
157	        printf 'tmux_status_run: no command after `--`\n' >&2
158	        return 1
159	    fi
160	
161	    # Capture target ONCE up front — if `cmd` happens to switch tmux
162	    # window, we still want the badge to land on the window the user
163	    # invoked from.
164	    _target=$(tmux display -p '#{session_name}:#{window_index}' 2>/dev/null)
165	    [ -z "$_target" ] && _target=""
166	
167	    # Trap so Ctrl+C / kill doesn't leak the working glyph forever.
168	    # Use a trap that clears, then re-raises the signal default for
169	    # correct exit semantics.
170	    trap '_tmux_status_run_trap "$_name" "$_target"' INT TERM HUP
171	
172	    tmux_status_set "$_name" "$_working" "$_target"
173	    "$@"
174	    _rc=$?
175	    if [ $_rc -eq 0 ]; then
176	        tmux_status_set "$_name" "$_ok" "$_target"
177	    else
178	        tmux_status_set "$_name" "$_fail" "$_target"
179	    fi
180	
181	    trap - INT TERM HUP
182	    return $_rc
183	}
184	
185	# Internal: trap helper for tmux_status_run. Clears the badge then
186	# re-raises the signal so the calling shell sees correct $? / exit code.
187	_tmux_status_run_trap() {
188	    tmux_status_clear "$1" "$2" 2>/dev/null
189	    trap - INT TERM HUP
190	    # Re-raise INT (most common case); for TERM/HUP we just let the
191	    # shell continue — calling scripts can decide what to do via $?.
192	    kill -INT $$ 2>/dev/null
193	}

7	# Auto-clone on first use (TPM only installs on prefix + I)
8	if-shell '[ ! -d ~/.tmux/plugins/tmux ]' \
9	  'run-shell "git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/catppuccin/tmux.git ~/.tmux/plugins/tmux 2>/dev/null"'
10	
11	# Top status bar, left-aligned window list
12	set -g status-position top
13	set -g status-justify left
14	
15	# Catppuccin options -- must be set BEFORE running the plugin
16	set -g @catppuccin_flavor 'mocha'
17	set -g @catppuccin_window_status_style 'rounded'
18	
19	# Window text (what each tab shows). #I = index, #W = window name.
20	# `#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}` appends the workmux per-window
21	# agent status emoji (🤖 working / 💬 waiting / ✅ done) when set. The
22	# variable is a tmux per-window user-option written by `workmux
23	# set-window-status` from Claude Code hooks (dot_claude/modify_settings.json)
24	# and the OpenCode plugin (dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts).
25	# `waiting` and `done` auto-clear on window focus; `working` is sticky and
26	# relies on `Stop` / `session.idle` hooks to transition to `done`. We set
27	# `status_format: false` in dot_config/workmux/config.yaml so workmux does
28	# NOT also append its own format per-tmux-session — that path is per-session
29	# and doesn't survive new sessions or chezmoi diffs. See
30	# docs/tools/workmux.md for the full integration story.
31	set -g @catppuccin_window_text ' #W#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}'
32	set -g @catppuccin_window_current_text ' #W#{?window_zoomed_flag, 󰊓 ,}#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}'
33	set -g @catppuccin_window_number_position 'left'
34	
35	# Module tweaks
36	set -g @catppuccin_directory_text "#{b:pane_current_path}"
37	set -g @catppuccin_date_time_text "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"
38	
39	# Load plugin -- this populates @catppuccin_status_*, window-status-format,
40	# window-status-current-format with Catppuccin styling
41	run '~/.tmux/plugins/tmux/catppuccin.tmux'
42	
43	# Responsive status line: status-left/status-right are conditional formats
44	# that select module bundles based on each client's #{client_width}, so
45	# multi-client attaches at different widths each see the right tier without
46	# stomping on each other.
47	run '~/.config/tmux/responsive.sh'
48	
49	# NOTE: intentionally do NOT override window-status-format /
50	# window-status-current-format here -- the plugin has already set those based
51	# on @catppuccin_window_status_style above, and overriding them with
52	# non-existent v1 variables wipes the window list.
53

1	# Workmux — tmux + git-worktree orchestration with agent status icons
2	
3	[Workmux](https://workmux.raine.dev) (`workmux` / `wm`) is a CLI from
4	[raine/workmux](https://github.com/raine/workmux) that ties tmux windows,
5	git worktrees, and AI coding agents into one workflow. It coexists with
6	[`worktrunk`](worktrunk.md) (`wt`) in this repo — the two solve overlapping
7	problems but each has a unique killer feature, so we keep both managed.
8	
9	> **TL;DR**
10	> - `wt` = worktree CLI / aliases / `wt cc fix-x -- 'prompt'` per-branch
11	>   Claude launcher. See [worktrunk playbook](worktrunk.md).
12	> - `wm` = same worktree-launcher concept BUT also: 🤖/💬/✅ icons in tmux
13	>   window list, `wm dashboard` TUI, `wm sidebar` always-on status pane,
14	>   per-window status user-var (`@workmux_status`).
15	> - This repo auto-installs both, manages `wm`'s status hooks for Claude
16	>   Code + OpenCode so the icons work on every fresh box, and patches the
17	>   upstream by-design `working` (🤖) leak so it doesn't get stuck.
18	
19	## Table of Contents
20	
21	- [Why both wt and wm?](#why-both-wt-and-wm)
22	- [What this repo manages for you](#what-this-repo-manages-for-you)
23	- [Status icon mechanics](#status-icon-mechanics)

25	- [Self-managed status format](#self-managed-status-format)
26	- [Daily commands](#daily-commands)

28	- [Sidebar daemon (optional)](#sidebar-daemon-optional)
29	- [Adding a new agent](#adding-a-new-agent)
30	- [Reusing the per-window status mechanism (without workmux)](#reusing-the-per-window-status-mechanism-without-workmux)
31	  - [Shell helpers: `tmux_status_*`](#shell-helpers-tmux_status_)
32	- [Cross-references](#cross-references)
33

35	
36	## Why both wt and wm?
37	
38	| Capability | `wt` (worktrunk) | `wm` (workmux) |
39	|---|---|---|
40	| Create worktree + branch + tmux pane | ✅ `wt switch -c -x claude feat` | ✅ `wm add feat` |
41	| Per-branch alias system | ✅ `[aliases]` in toml | ⚠️ named layouts only |
42	| Cleanup `merge`/`remove` lifecycle | ✅ | ✅ |
43	| Hooks (pre/post-start/merge/remove) | ✅ ten hook types | ✅ four hook types |
44	| Tmux window-status agent icon | ❌ no integration | ✅ `@workmux_status` |
45	| Always-visible status sidebar | ❌ | ✅ `wm sidebar` |
46	| Dashboard TUI (`d` for diff, `c` for commit) | ⚠️ interactive picker only | ✅ `wm dashboard` |
47	| Sandbox (Docker / Lima / Apple Container) | ❌ | ✅ |
48	| LLM commit messages | ✅ `wt merge` invokes LLM | ❌ |
49	| Auto-detected backend (kitty / wezterm / zellij) | ⚠️ tmux-only | ✅ multi-backend |
50	| Already in this repo | since 2026-04 | since 2026-05-11 |
51	
52	You don't have to use both. The split is:
53	
54	- **`wt cc <branch> -- 'prompt'`** stays the muscle-memory entry for
55	  parallel Claude/OpenCode in a worktree (worktrunk's alias engine is more
56	  expressive).
57	- **`wm` is what gives you the 🤖/💬/✅ icons** in the tmux window list, no
58	  matter which tool you used to spawn the agent. The icons come from
59	  workmux hooks installed in Claude/OpenCode that run regardless of which
60	  CLI you used to launch them.
61	- **`wm dashboard` / `wm sidebar`** for monitoring N parallel agents.
62	
63	If you only want one, drop `wt`'s aliases from
64	[`dot_config/worktrunk/config.toml`](../../dot_config/worktrunk/config.toml)
65	and use `wm add -x claude` in its place.
66	
67	## What this repo manages for you
68	
69	| File / setting | Path | Purpose |
70	|---|---|---|
71	| Binary install (macOS) | `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` (`workmux` in `homebrew:` list, `raine/workmux` tap) | `brew install workmux` on every macOS apply |
72	| Binary install (Linux) | `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` (workmux block) | Downloads `workmux-linux-{amd64,arm64}.tar.gz` from GitHub releases to `~/.local/bin/`; symlinks `wm -> workmux` |
73	| Global config | [`dot_config/workmux/config.yaml`](../../dot_config/workmux/config.yaml) | `nerdfont: false` + `status_format: false` (we manage the tmux format ourselves) |
74	| Tmux window format | [`dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf`](../../dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf) | Appends `#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}` to `@catppuccin_window_text` / `@catppuccin_window_current_text` |
75	| Claude hooks | [`dot_claude/modify_settings.json`](../../dot_claude/modify_settings.json) | Adds `Stop` / `SubagentStop` / `UserPromptSubmit` / `Notification` hooks calling `workmux set-window-status` |
76	| OpenCode plugin | [`dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts`](../../dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts) | Vendored copy of upstream plugin — listens to OpenCode events, calls `workmux set-window-status` |
77	| OpenCode plugin deps | [`dot_config/opencode/modify_package.json`](../../dot_config/opencode/modify_package.json) | jq-merges `@opencode-ai/plugin: 1.4.3` into existing `package.json` |
78	| Shell helpers | [`dot_config/zsh/tools/38_workmux.zsh`](../../dot_config/zsh/tools/38_workmux.zsh) | `wmclear` (manual marker reset), `wmsb` alias, `wm='workmux'` fallback alias |
79	
80	What is **NOT** managed (by design):
81	
82	- `wm setup` is not auto-run. It would write the same Claude/OpenCode hooks
83	  we already manage above, leading to duplicate entries (the hook-aware
84	  merger in `modify_settings.json` would deduplicate them but the cleaner
85	  path is to skip `wm setup` entirely on managed machines). On a fresh box
86	  the chezmoi layer installs everything `wm setup` would have done.
87	- `~/.config/workmux/state/` (per-machine runtime state — XDG state dir).
88	- `wm dashboard` color theme overrides — defaults are fine.
89	- Per-project `.workmux.yaml` — that lives in each project repo, not here.
90	
91	## Status icon mechanics
92	
93	Three states, three glyphs (defaults):
94	
95	| State | Glyph | Set by | Auto-clear behaviour |
96	|---|---|---|---|
97	| `working` | 🤖 | Agent processing a turn | ❌ **Sticky** — never auto-clears |
98	| `waiting` | 💬 | Permission prompt / question | ✅ Clears when window receives focus |
99	| `done` | ✅ | Turn finished gracefully | ✅ Clears when window receives focus |
100	| `clear` | (none) | Explicit unset | — |
101	
102	The mechanism: `workmux set-window-status <state>` writes to the tmux
103	**per-window user option** `@workmux_status` for the current window. Our
104	catppuccin format string appends `#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}`,
105	so any window with the option set renders the glyph after `#W`.
106	
107	Verify on a live tmux:
108	
109	```bash
110	# See which windows have the marker set
111	tmux list-windows -aF '#{session_name}:#{window_index} #{@workmux_status}'
112	
113	# Look at the format string our theme installed
114	tmux show -gv @catppuccin_window_text
115	# Expected: ' #W#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}'
116	```
117	
118	## The 🤖-leak problem and how we fix it
119	
120	`working` is **sticky by design** — it only transitions away when the agent
121	explicitly calls `set-window-status done` (or `clear`). When the agent dies
122	ungracefully (Ctrl+C, terminal crash, OOM, SSH disconnect), no `done` ever
123	fires and the 🤖 sticks forever.
124	
125	Worse for Claude specifically: upstream's default `wm setup` only installs
126	hooks that **set** `working` (`PostToolUse`, `UserPromptSubmit`) — there is
127	no `Stop` hook calling `set-window-status done`. Every Claude turn ends with
128	🤖 still showing. This is **by design** in upstream and was the root cause
129	of the [original investigation](../../pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md).
130	
131	This repo fixes both leak modes:
132	
133	1. **Claude `Stop` + `SubagentStop` hooks** — managed in
134	   [`dot_claude/modify_settings.json`](../../dot_claude/modify_settings.json).
135	   Every Claude turn end calls `workmux set-window-status done`, which
136	   immediately makes ✅ appear and then auto-clears on focus. Fixes the
137	   by-design leak.
138	
139	2. **OpenCode `session.idle` event handler** — vendored from upstream into
140	   [`dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts`](../../dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts).
141	   This works for graceful shutdowns. Crash/Ctrl+C still leaks.
142	
143	3. **Crash leak (any agent)** — three escape hatches:
144	   - `workmux sidebar` running anywhere → 10s pane-silence detection
145	     auto-downgrades stuck `working` to interrupted (released v0.1.99 +
146	     v0.1.163). See [Sidebar daemon (optional)](#sidebar-daemon-optional).
147	   - `wmclear` (this repo's helper) — manual reset. See
148	     [Manual cleanup](#manual-cleanup-wmclear).
149	   - `command -v workmux >/dev/null && workmux set-window-status clear` —
150	     raw command if you forget the alias.
```

Perfect. Now I have all the information. Let me compile my findings:

## Report: Workmux Per-Window Status Icon Flow & Manual Bookmark Integration

### A. **Current data flow**

The 🤖/💬/✅ status icon reaches the tmux status line through a 3-stage pipeline:

1. **Source (hooks)**: Claude Code's `Stop`/`SubagentStop`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`Notification` hooks fire and call:
   ```
   command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && workmux set-window-status <state> || true
   ```
   (from `dot_claude/modify_settings.json` lines 59, 70, 88, 98)

2. **Storage (tmux per-window user option)**: `workmux set-window-status` writes to the tmux **per-window user-option** named `@workmux_status` via the equivalent of:
   ```bash
   tmux set-option -w '@workmux_status' '🤖'  # (or 💬 / ✅)
   ```

3. **Render (theme format string)**: The catppuccin theme evaluates a **conditional expansion** in its window-text format:
   ```tmux
   set -g @catppuccin_window_text ' #W#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}'
   set -g @catppuccin_window_current_text ' #W#{?window_zoomed_flag, 󰊓 ,}#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}'
   ```
   (lines 31–32 of `theme.catppuccin.conf`)

   The `#{?@workmux_status, …, }` syntax means: "if `@workmux_status` is set, render ` #{@workmux_status}` (space + value); otherwise render nothing."

The POSIX shell helpers in `60_tmux_status.sh` (lines 68–107) wrap this with the canonical command pattern:
```bash
tmux set-option -w [-t TARGET] "@${_name}_status" "$_glyph"  # set
tmux set-option -w [-t TARGET] -u "@${_name}_status"        # unset
```

---

### B. **Per-window option naming: current & reserved**

**Currently in use:**
- `@workmux_status` — exclusive; reserved by the validation in `60_tmux_status.sh:53` (rejects names starting with `workmux*`)
- `@catppuccin_*` — theme variables (flavor, window text, styles, etc.); these are **global** options, not per-window
- `@theme_variant` — global, for theme selection

**Safe naming for your bookmark feature:**
The validation in `60_tmux_status.sh:47–64` enforces:
- Names must match `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+`
- Names starting with `workmux` are rejected
- Empty names are rejected

**Recommended name:** `@bookmark` or `@bookmark_status` (follows the `@<tool>_status` convention from line 451 of `workmux.md`). Alternatively: `@pinned`, `@manual_mark`, `@tag_status`. The validation will accept any of these since none start with `workmux`.

---

### C. **Status format combinability: yes, fully supported**

Both window-text format strings **support concatenating multiple conditionals**. The current theme already demonstrates the pattern (line 32):
```tmux
' #W#{?window_zoomed_flag, 󰊓 ,}#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}'
```

This chains two conditionals in sequence. To add your bookmark:
```tmux
set -g @catppuccin_window_text ' #W#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}#{?@bookmark, ★,}'
set -g @catppuccin_window_current_text ' #W#{?window_zoomed_flag, 󰊓 ,}#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}#{?@bookmark, ★,}'
```

Result: window shows `zsh 🤖 ★` when both agent and bookmark are set, `zsh 🤖` for agent-only, `zsh ★` for bookmark-only, `zsh` for neither.

---

### D. **Manual clear surface: yes, `wmclear` + generic helpers**

**Existing workmux-specific escape hatch:**
- `wmclear` — function in `38_workmux.sh:39–73` clears `@workmux_status` for current window, a specific window, or all windows in session
- Direct command: `workmux set-window-status clear` (calls `wmclear` for current window; prefers this to preserve workmux's internal agent state)

**Generic POSIX helpers for your bookmark:**
The `60_tmux_status.sh` module already exports:
```bash
tmux_status_set bookmark '★' [mysession:3]    # set bookmark on current or target window
tmux_status_clear bookmark [mysession:3]       # unset bookmark on current or target window
tmux_status_clear_all bookmark                 # unset across every session
tmux_status_list                               # audit all @*_status across all windows
tmux_status_get bookmark                       # read current window's bookmark value
```

No pre-existing shell alias or binding for `bookmark` yet—you'd add one (e.g., `bmtoggle`, `bmclear`), but the primitives are ready.

---

### E. **Hard rules from the 6-file invariant (from CLAUDE.md)**

The workmux integration spans exactly **6 surfaces**. Quoting the CLAUDE.md "Hard rules":

> Never run `workmux setup` on a managed machine (would write parallel hook entries); never flip `status_format: true` (fights catppuccin's window-text override); never drop the `command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && … || true` guard in Claude hooks (spams errors on fresh boxes); never drop explicit `set-window-status done` from `Stop`/`SubagentStop` (upstream only ever sets `working`, never clears — that's the by-design leak).

2. ✅ `command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && … || true` guards present on all 4 hook entries (`modify_settings.json:59, 70, 88, 98`)
3. ✅ Both `Stop` and `SubagentStop` hooks call `set-window-status done` (`modify_settings.json:88, 98`)
4. ✅ `workmux setup` is **never** run—all hooks are vendored into chezmoi

**Safe additions for your manual-bookmark menu:**

Hand-rolled tmux commands in a menu binding (e.g., in `menu-agents.sh` or a new `menu-bookmarks.sh`) are 100% safe as long as they:

1. **Call `tmux_status_set bookmark …` or raw `tmux set-option -w @bookmark …`** instead of touching `@workmux_status`
2. **Never flip `status_format: true`** (don't modify workmux config)
3. **Never call `workmux setup`** (don't invite parallel hook rewrites)

5. **Preserve the `command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1` guard** if you call workmux from hooks (not needed for menu bindings, which run interactively in tmux)

The `60_tmux_status.sh` validation **already reserves** `workmux*` prefixes, so collision is impossible by design.

12	# Why a separate file from 37_worktrunk.{sh,zsh}: the two tools coexist

14	# icons + dashboard + sidebar). Separate files keep the rationale + helpers
15	# per-tool and let users disable one independently.

20	
21	# ── Manual marker cleanup ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
22	#
23	# The `working` (🤖) status workmux sets is *sticky* — it never auto-clears
24	# on its own. `waiting` (💬) and `done` (✅) auto-clear when you focus the
25	# window, but `working` only goes away when:
26	#   1. The agent's plugin/hook explicitly calls `workmux set-window-status done`
27	#      (Claude Stop / OpenCode session.idle), OR
28	#   2. `workmux sidebar` is running and detects 10s of pane silence
29	#      (interrupted-agent detection), OR
30	#   3. You manually clear it.
31	#
32	# Path #1 fails when the agent is killed before its Stop/idle handler fires
33	# (Ctrl+C, terminal crash, OOM). Path #2 requires keeping a sidebar pane open.
34	# `wmclear` is the manual escape hatch.
35	#
36	# Without arg: clears the marker for the current tmux window.
37	# With arg:    `wmclear 5` clears window 5 in the current session.
38	# Pass `--all` to nuke every workmux marker in the current session.
39	function wmclear() {
40	    if [[ "$1" == "--all" ]]; then
41	        # Walk every window in the current session and unset the user-var.
42	        # Original zsh code used `windows=("${(@f)$(...)}")` to split command
43	        # output on newlines; the `while IFS= read -r` loop below is the
44	        # portable equivalent (works in bash + zsh).
45	        local sess
46	        sess=$(tmux display -p '#{session_name}' 2>/dev/null) || return 1
47	        local -a windows
48	        windows=()
49	        local w
50	        while IFS= read -r w; do
51	            [ -n "$w" ] && windows+=( "$w" )
52	        done < <(tmux list-windows -t "$sess" -F '#{window_index}' 2>/dev/null)
53	        for w in "${windows[@]}"; do
54	            tmux set-option -w -t "${sess}:${w}" -u '@workmux_status' 2>/dev/null
55	        done
56	        echo "Cleared @workmux_status on ${#windows[@]} windows in session $sess"
57	        return 0
58	    fi
59	
60	    if [[ -n "$1" ]]; then
61	        # Specific window: use workmux's own clear command (handles agent
62	        # state too, not just the tmux user-var)
63	        local sess win
64	        sess=$(tmux display -p '#{session_name}' 2>/dev/null) || return 1
65	        win="$1"
66	        tmux set-option -w -t "${sess}:${win}" -u '@workmux_status' 2>/dev/null
67	        echo "Cleared @workmux_status on ${sess}:${win}"
68	        return 0
69	    fi
70	
71	    # Current window: prefer workmux's clear so it also resets agent state
72	    workmux set-window-status clear 2>/dev/null
73	}
74	
75	# ── Sidebar daemon convenience ─────────────────────────────────────────────
76	#
77	# `workmux sidebar` is what enables the "interrupted agent" auto-clear (10s
78	# pane-silence heuristic). Without it, `working` markers leak forever on
79	# crashed agents. NOT auto-started here because it spawns a tmux pane and
80	# many users want to opt-in. Use `wmsb` to toggle.
81	alias wmsb='workmux sidebar'
82	
83	# ── Short aliases mirroring upstream's recommendation ──────────────────────
84	# README explicitly suggests `alias wm='workmux'`. The Linux ansible install
85	# also creates a `wm` symlink in ~/.local/bin so this alias is redundant on
86	# Linux, but on macOS Homebrew installs only `workmux`, so define it here.
87	if ! command -v wm &>/dev/null; then
88	    alias wm='workmux'
89	fi
90

## Summary

**Right-click (MouseDown3Status) menu location and status:**

The right-click tab/window menu is **NOT using a custom menu** — it's fully **built-in to tmux**, but **customized via keybindings**:

**File:** `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl`  
**Binding:** Lines 48–80 (unbind-key -n MouseDown3Status, then bind-key -n MouseDown3Status)

The menu is **completely defined inline** with `display-menu -O` (the `-O` flag makes it stay open after click release). The menu items match your screenshot exactly:
- Swap Left/Right (lines 63–64)
- Even horizontal/vertical, Main horizontal/vertical, Tiled (lines 66–70)
- Move/Link to session (lines 72–73)
- Break all panes → windows (line 74, calls `~/.config/tmux/break-all-panes.sh`)
- Kill window, Renumber, Rename, New window (lines 76–80)

**No other files override or modify this menu** — all `menu-*.sh` scripts are for the **prefix+Space popup menu** (not right-click tabs), called from `executable_menu.sh`.

---

## Workmux Data Flow

**Config:** `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/workmux/config.yaml`  
**Status helper API:** `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh`  
**Manual clear helper:** `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/shell/38_workmux.sh` (the `wmclear` function)

**The flow:**

1. **workmux writes to per-window user-var** `@workmux_status` via:
   ```bash
   workmux set-window-status <state>  # state = working|waiting|done|clear
   # Internally: tmux set-option -w '@workmux_status' '<glyph>'
   ```

2. **Catppuccin theme reads and renders it** (`theme.catppuccin.conf`, lines 31–32):
   ```
   set -g @catppuccin_window_text ' #W#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}'
   ```
   Format string: `#W` (window name) + conditional `#{?@workmux_status, <emoji>,}` (append emoji if set, else empty)

3. **Claude Code + OpenCode hooks call** `workmux set-window-status`:
   - Claude: `dot_claude/modify_settings.json` (Stop / SubagentStop / UserPromptSubmit hooks)
   - OpenCode: `dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts` (vendored plugin)

4. **Public API for non-agent producers:** `dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh`
   ```bash
   tmux_status_set my_build 🔨              # set per-window var @my_build_status
   tmux_status_get my_build                 # read it
   tmux_status_clear my_build               # unset it
   tmux_status_clear_all my_build           # unset across all windows
   tmux_status_run my_build 🔨 ✅ ❌ -- cmd # run cmd with badges
   ```

5. **Manual clearing:** `wmclear` (38_workmux.sh, lines 39–73)
   ```bash
   wmclear           # clear current window's @workmux_status
   wmclear 5         # clear window 5's @workmux_status
   wmclear --all     # clear every window in the session
   ```

---

## Current Per-Window Variables

**Only `@workmux_status` is in active use** for per-window badges. No other per-window `@*_status` vars exist.

Global session vars (not per-window): `@catppuccin_status_*`, `@_status_left_*`, `@_status_right_*` (in `responsive.sh`), but these are **session-level**, not per-window.

---

## Design Conflicts / Overlap

**No conflicts** between your proposed additions and workmux:

1. **wmclear menu item**: Can coexist perfectly. It would call `tmux_status_clear workmux` (or `workmux set-window-status clear`) on the right-clicked window — the menu has `#{window_id}` available, so you can target it directly.

2. **Bookmark toggle icon** (`@bookmark_status` or `@pinned_status`): Can render **alongside** `@workmux_status` without overwriting it. Modify the theme format on lines 31–32 of `theme.catppuccin.conf`:
   ```
   ' #W#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}#{?@bookmark_status, #{@bookmark_status},}'
   ```
   Both glyphs render in sequence: `window 🤖 ⭐` (agent working + bookmarked).

**Naming convention:** Use the public API layer (60_tmux_status.sh). Call it with a name like `bookmark` or `pinned`:
```bash
tmux_status_set bookmark ⭐           # tag current window
tmux_status_get bookmark              # check if set
tmux_status_clear bookmark            # remove bookmark
```
This keeps the namespace tidy (`@<name>_status` everywhere) and lets you grep for "every status producer" with `tmux_status_list`.

54	# so on small terminals (mobile SSH, half-height splits) this menu may not
55	# appear. Layouts are inlined here (rather than via a submenu) because
56	# nested display-menu chained through `run-shell` had unreliable mouse-event
57	# behaviour — see pitfalls/tmux-submenu-flash-and-bottom-right.md.

59	# the prefix+Enter popup: Renumber windows (covered by `prefix + r`),
60	# the less-used Main horizontal/vertical layouts.

63	    "Swap Left"  l { swap-window -t :-1 } \
64	    "Swap Right" r { swap-window -t :+1 } \
65	    "" \
66	    "Even horizontal" 1 { select-layout even-horizontal } \

79	    "" \
80	    "New window"  w { new-window }
81	
82	unbind-key -n MouseDown3StatusLeft
83	bind-key -n MouseDown3StatusLeft \

1	# ~/.config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh
2	# Source: dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh (managed by chezmoi)
3	#
4	# Generic per-window tmux status badge helpers — POSIX, sourced by both
5	# zsh and bash. Thin convenience layer over the same primitive workmux
6	# uses (`tmux set-option -w '@<name>_status' '<glyph>'`), so any script /
7	# hook / cron job / build watcher can tag its tmux window without
8	# pulling in workmux.
9	#
10	# Why a shared layer (not in 38_workmux.zsh): these helpers don't need
11	# any zsh feature, and the most common consumers (build scripts, deploy
12	# hooks, CI wrappers) tend to be `#!/bin/bash` or `#!/bin/sh`. Putting
13	# them in dot_config/shell/ means they Just Work from any shell.
14	#
15	# Companion: docs/tools/workmux.md → "Reusing the per-window status
16	# mechanism (without workmux)" for design rationale, the lifecycle hard
17	# rules, and the build-watcher worked example.
18	#
19	# Quick reference:
20	#
21	#   tmux_status_set my_build 🔨           # tag current window
22	#   tmux_status_set my_build 🔨 mysess:3  # tag specific window
23	#   tmux_status_get my_build              # read current window
24	#   tmux_status_clear my_build            # unset (current window)
25	#   tmux_status_clear my_build mysess:3   # unset specific window
26	#   tmux_status_clear_all my_build        # unset across every session
27	#   tmux_status_list                      # list every @*_status user-var
28	#   tmux_status_run my_build 🔨 ✅ ❌ -- npm run build
29	#                                         # set 🔨, run cmd, set ✅/❌
30	#                                         # by exit code, auto-clear on
31	#                                         # signal trap
32	#
33	# Naming convention: pass the LOGICAL name without `@` or `_status`
34	# suffix — these helpers add the `@<name>_status` wrapper. So
35	# `tmux_status_set my_build 🔨` writes `@my_build_status`. This keeps
36	# the user-var namespace tidy (`@<tool>_status` everywhere) and lets
37	# you grep for "every status producer" with `tmux_status_list`.
38	
39	# Skip silently if tmux isn't on PATH (cron, headless SSH, fresh box
40	# pre-ansible). Producers can call these unconditionally.
41	command -v tmux >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0

43	# Internal: validate name (alphanumeric + underscore + dash, no `@` /
44	# `_status` since we add them). Returns 0 if valid, 1 if not (with
45	# stderr diagnostic). Empty name is rejected. Names starting with
46	# `workmux` are reserved to avoid clobbering workmux's own user-var.
47	_tmux_status_validate_name() {
48	    if [ -z "${1:-}" ]; then
49	        printf 'tmux_status: name argument is required\n' >&2
50	        return 1
51	    fi
52	    case "$1" in
53	        workmux*)
54	            # shellcheck disable=SC2016 # Backticks here are literal Markdown-style code spans, not command substitution.
55	            printf 'tmux_status: name "%s" reserved (workmux owns @workmux_status). Use `workmux set-window-status` for the agent path.\n' "$1" >&2
56	            return 1
57	            ;;
58	        *[!A-Za-z0-9_-]*)
59	            printf 'tmux_status: name "%s" must be [A-Za-z0-9_-]+\n' "$1" >&2
60	            return 1
61	            ;;
62	    esac
63	    return 0
64	}

66	# tmux_status_set <name> <glyph> [target]
67	#   target defaults to current window (`tmux display -p '#{session_name}:#{window_index}'`)
68	tmux_status_set() {
69	    _tmux_status_validate_name "${1:-}" || return 1
70	    if [ $# -lt 2 ]; then
71	        printf 'tmux_status_set: usage: tmux_status_set <name> <glyph> [target]\n' >&2
72	        return 1
73	    fi
74	    _name="$1"
75	    _glyph="$2"
76	    _target="${3:-}"

78	        tmux set-option -w -t "$_target" "@${_name}_status" "$_glyph" 2>/dev/null
79	    else

81	    fi

92	    else
93	        tmux show-options -wv "@${_name}_status" 2>/dev/null
94	    fi
95	}
96	
97	# tmux_status_clear <name> [target]
98	tmux_status_clear() {
99	    _tmux_status_validate_name "${1:-}" || return 1
100	    _name="$1"
101	    _target="${2:-}"

103	        tmux set-option -w -t "$_target" -u "@${_name}_status" 2>/dev/null
104	    else

106	    fi
107	}

109	# tmux_status_clear_all <name>
110	#   walk every window in every session, unset @<name>_status
111	tmux_status_clear_all() {
112	    _tmux_status_validate_name "${1:-}" || return 1
113	    _name="$1"
114	    tmux list-windows -aF '#{session_name}:#{window_index}' 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r _w; do
115	        tmux set-option -w -t "$_w" -u "@${_name}_status" 2>/dev/null
116	    done
117	}

119	# tmux_status_list
120	#   show every @*_status user-var across every window (read-only audit)
121	tmux_status_list() {
122	    tmux list-windows -aF '#{session_name}:#{window_index} #{window_name}' 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r _line; do
123	        _w="${_line%% *}"
124	        # Pull every option starting with @ on this window, filter to *_status
125	        tmux show-options -w -t "$_w" 2>/dev/null \
126	            | awk -v w="$_line" '/^@[A-Za-z0-9_-]+_status / {print w "  " $0}'
127	    done

130	# tmux_status_run <name> <working_glyph> <ok_glyph> <fail_glyph> -- <cmd> [args...]
131	#   Run a command, badge the window with `working_glyph` while it runs,
132	#   then `ok_glyph` on success or `fail_glyph` on failure. Traps INT /
133	#   TERM / HUP to clear the badge instead of leaking on Ctrl+C.
134	#
135	#   Example:
136	#     tmux_status_run my_build 🔨 ✅ ❌ -- npm run build
137	#     tmux_status_run deploy   🚀 🟢 🔴 -- ./deploy.sh prod
138	tmux_status_run() {
139	    _tmux_status_validate_name "${1:-}" || return 1
140	    if [ $# -lt 6 ]; then
141	        printf 'tmux_status_run: usage: tmux_status_run <name> <working> <ok> <fail> -- <cmd> [args...]\n' >&2
142	        return 1
143	    fi
144	    _name="$1"
145	    _working="$2"
146	    _ok="$3"
147	    _fail="$4"
148	    shift 4
149	    if [ "${1:-}" != "--" ]; then
150	        # shellcheck disable=SC2016 # Backticks are literal in the diagnostic message.
151	        printf 'tmux_status_run: missing `--` separator before command\n' >&2
152	        return 1
153	    fi
154	    shift
155	    if [ $# -eq 0 ]; then
156	        # shellcheck disable=SC2016 # Backticks are literal in the diagnostic message.
157	        printf 'tmux_status_run: no command after `--`\n' >&2
158	        return 1
159	    fi
160	
161	    # Capture target ONCE up front — if `cmd` happens to switch tmux
162	    # window, we still want the badge to land on the window the user
163	    # invoked from.
164	    _target=$(tmux display -p '#{session_name}:#{window_index}' 2>/dev/null)
165	    [ -z "$_target" ] && _target=""
166	
167	    # Trap so Ctrl+C / kill doesn't leak the working glyph forever.
168	    # Use a trap that clears, then re-raises the signal default for
169	    # correct exit semantics.
170	    trap '_tmux_status_run_trap "$_name" "$_target"' INT TERM HUP
171	
172	    tmux_status_set "$_name" "$_working" "$_target"
173	    "$@"
174	    _rc=$?
175	    if [ $_rc -eq 0 ]; then
176	        tmux_status_set "$_name" "$_ok" "$_target"
177	    else
178	        tmux_status_set "$_name" "$_fail" "$_target"
179	    fi
180	
181	    trap - INT TERM HUP
182	    return $_rc
183	}
184	
185	# Internal: trap helper for tmux_status_run. Clears the badge then
186	# re-raises the signal so the calling shell sees correct $? / exit code.
187	_tmux_status_run_trap() {
188	    tmux_status_clear "$1" "$2" 2>/dev/null
189	    trap - INT TERM HUP
190	    # Re-raise INT (most common case); for TERM/HUP we just let the
191	    # shell continue — calling scripts can decide what to do via $?.
192	    kill -INT $$ 2>/dev/null
193	}

```text
1	# 38_workmux.sh - Workmux (`workmux` / `wm`) tmux + git-worktree orchestrator
2	# (shared bash + zsh). Moved from dot_config/zsh/tools/38_workmux.zsh; the
3	# only zsh-ism was `${(@f)$(cmd)}` (split-on-newlines flag), rewritten as a
4	# `while IFS= read -r` loop.
5	#
6	# https://workmux.raine.dev — github.com/raine/workmux
7	#
8	# Companion config: ~/.config/workmux/config.yaml (managed by chezmoi at
9	# dot_config/workmux/config.yaml). See docs/tools/workmux.md for the full
10	# story (worktrunk vs workmux split, status icon lifecycle, leak mitigation).
11	#
12	# Why a separate file from 37_worktrunk.{sh,zsh}: the two tools coexist
13	# (worktrunk = `wt` for git-worktree CLI / aliases, workmux = `wm` for status
14	# icons + dashboard + sidebar). Separate files keep the rationale + helpers
15	# per-tool and let users disable one independently.
16	
17	# Skip silently if not installed (Linux ansible install can fail offline,
18	# Cargo path may not be present, etc.)
19	command -v workmux &>/dev/null || return 0
20	
21	# ── Manual marker cleanup ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
22	#
23	# The `working` (🤖) status workmux sets is *sticky* — it never auto-clears
24	# on its own. `waiting` (💬) and `done` (✅) auto-clear when you focus the
25	# window, but `working` only goes away when:
26	#   1. The agent's plugin/hook explicitly calls `workmux set-window-status done`
27	#      (Claude Stop / OpenCode session.idle), OR
28	#   2. `workmux sidebar` is running and detects 10s of pane silence
29	#      (interrupted-agent detection), OR
30	#   3. You manually clear it.
31	#
32	# Path #1 fails when the agent is killed before its Stop/idle handler fires
33	# (Ctrl+C, terminal crash, OOM). Path #2 requires keeping a sidebar pane open.
34	# `wmclear` is the manual escape hatch.
35	#
36	# Without arg: clears the marker for the current tmux window.
37	# With arg:    `wmclear 5` clears window 5 in the current session.
38	# Pass `--all` to nuke every workmux marker in the current session.
39	function wmclear() {
40	    if [[ "$1" == "--all" ]]; then
41	        # Walk every window in the current session and unset the user-var.
42	        # Original zsh code used `windows=("${(@f)$(...)}")` to split command
43	        # output on newlines; the `while IFS= read -r` loop below is the
44	        # portable equivalent (works in bash + zsh).
45	        local sess
46	        sess=$(tmux display -p '#{session_name}' 2>/dev/null) || return 1
47	        local -a windows
48	        windows=()
49	        local w
50	        while IFS= read -r w; do
51	            [ -n "$w" ] && windows+=( "$w" )
52	        done < <(tmux list-windows -t "$sess" -F '#{window_index}' 2>/dev/null)
53	        for w in "${windows[@]}"; do
54	            tmux set-option -w -t "${sess}:${w}" -u '@workmux_status' 2>/dev/null
55	        done
56	        echo "Cleared @workmux_status on ${#windows[@]} windows in session $sess"
57	        return 0
58	    fi
59	
60	    if [[ -n "$1" ]]; then
61	        # Specific window: use workmux's own clear command (handles agent
62	        # state too, not just the tmux user-var)
63	        local sess win
64	        sess=$(tmux display -p '#{session_name}' 2>/dev/null) || return 1
65	        win="$1"
66	        tmux set-option -w -t "${sess}:${win}" -u '@workmux_status' 2>/dev/null
67	        echo "Cleared @workmux_status on ${sess}:${win}"
68	        return 0
69	    fi
70	
71	    # Current window: prefer workmux's clear so it also resets agent state
72	    workmux set-window-status clear 2>/dev/null
73	}
74	
75	# ── Sidebar daemon convenience ─────────────────────────────────────────────
76	#
77	# `workmux sidebar` is what enables the "interrupted agent" auto-clear (10s
78	# pane-silence heuristic). Without it, `working` markers leak forever on
79	# crashed agents. NOT auto-started here because it spawns a tmux pane and
80	# many users want to opt-in. Use `wmsb` to toggle.
81	alias wmsb='workmux sidebar'
82	
83	# ── Short aliases mirroring upstream's recommendation ──────────────────────
84	# README explicitly suggests `alias wm='workmux'`. The Linux ansible install
85	# also creates a `wm` symlink in ~/.local/bin so this alias is redundant on
86	# Linux, but on macOS Homebrew installs only `workmux`, so define it here.
87	if ! command -v wm &>/dev/null; then
88	    alias wm='workmux'
89	fi
90
```

```text
1	# tmux: nested display-menu via `run-shell` from a right-click parent menu is unreliable
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section): submenu flashes and disappears, popup in bottom-right corner, `display-menu` flickers, right-click submenu won't stay open, tmux menu position wrong from status bar, submenu opens but selecting an item does nothing on second invocation
4	**First seen**: 2026-04
5	**Affects**: tmux 3.3+ (likely older too); any `display-menu` invoked indirectly via `run-shell "$HOME/.config/tmux/menu-foo.sh"` from a `MouseDown3*` parent
6	**Status**: workaround — inline the submenu items into the parent instead of nesting via shell script
7	
8	## Symptom
9	
10	A `tmux display-menu` submenu (e.g. `~/.config/tmux/menu-layouts.sh`) behaves
11	two different ways depending on how it's invoked:
12	
13	- From a keyboard popup menu (e.g. `prefix + Enter` → "Layouts..."): opens
14	  near the cursor / pane center, stays open until an item is chosen. **Works.**
15	- From a **right-click status-bar** menu (e.g. right-click window tab →
16	  "Layouts..."): pops up in the **bottom-right corner of the terminal** and
17	  often **flashes away after a fraction of a second** before any item can be
18	  picked. Sometimes (if you happen to mouse over a row immediately) it stays.
19	
20	No error in `tmux show-messages`. The bind is correctly wired — `prefix +
21	Enter` path proves the script runs.
22	
23	## Root cause
24	
25	Two unrelated `display-menu` quirks stacked on top of each other:
26	
27	### 1. Mouse-release dismiss (the "flash and gone")
28	
29	A submenu without `-O` closes on the **next mouse event** that isn't a hover.
30	The right-click on the parent window-tab generated a pending mouse-release /
31	mouse-move event in tmux's event queue. The parent menu used `-O` (Open)
32	so it survived; the submenu didn't, so the queued release event hit it
33	immediately and dismissed it. With keyboard invocation there is no pending
34	mouse event, so the same submenu stayed open.
35	
36	### 2. `-x R -y P` from a status-bar event lands at bottom-right
37	
38	`-x R` = right edge of the pane. `-y P` = the line of the cursor's pane.
39	When `display-menu` is launched from a `MouseDown3Status` binding, "the
40	cursor's pane line" resolves to the **status bar row** (very bottom of the
41	terminal). Combined with `-x R` you get a popup glued to the bottom-right
42	corner. tmux 3.3+ then clamps it to fit on screen, which makes it look
43	"stuck" there. From a keyboard popup the cursor is in a normal pane, so the
44	same `-x R -y P` puts the menu in a sensible place near the parent.
45	
46	`man tmux` on `display-menu`:
47	> `M` for the mouse position, `W` for the window position on the status line,
48	> `S` for the line above or below the status line, `C` for the centre of the
49	> client.
50	
51	## Fix
52	
53	**Don't nest.** Inline the submenu items directly into the parent menu, even
54	if it pushes the parent above the ~14-row soft cap (see
55	`AGENTS.md` → "tmux ≥ 3.3 required for popup menu"). The cap exists for a
56	real reason (small terminals silently suppress oversized menus), so when
57	inlining grows the parent past 14 rows, drop the lowest-frequency rows and
58	move them to the keyboard popup (`prefix + Enter` → submenu) where the
59	nesting works fine.
60	
61	```tmux
62	# Bad: nested via run-shell (selection silently no-ops on 2nd invocation)
63	bind-key -n MouseDown3Status display-menu -O ... \
64	  "Layouts..." L { run-shell "~/.config/tmux/menu-layouts.sh" } \
65	  ...
66	
67	# Good: inline the layout commands directly
68	bind-key -n MouseDown3Status display-menu -O ... \
69	  "Even horizontal" 1 { select-layout even-horizontal } \
70	  "Even vertical"   2 { select-layout even-vertical } \
71	  "Tiled (grid)"    5 { select-layout tiled } \
72	  ...
73	```
74	
75	The keyboard popup path (`prefix + Enter` → "Layouts..." → `run-shell
76	~/.config/tmux/menu-layouts.sh`) keeps working — the bug is specific to
77	mouse-driven parents whose mouse-event lifecycle interferes with the child
78	menu's input handling.
79	
80	## Things that look like fixes but aren't
81	
82	Spent time trying these — none worked reliably across "first invocation"
83	vs "after cancelling once":
84	
85	- `-O` on the submenu: stops the immediate flash-and-gone, but on second
86	  invocation after cancelling the parent, selecting an item silently
87	  no-ops.
88	- `-x M -y M` on the submenu: fixes the bottom-right placement, but mouse
89	  position state is stale after cancel-and-retry, so it pops up in
90	  unpredictable places.
91	- `run-shell -d 0.1 "~/.config/tmux/menu-foo.sh"`: deferring the shell
92	  exec lets the parent's mouse-release drain, fixes the flash, but the
93	  selection-no-ops bug remains.
94	- `display-popup` wrapping the submenu: changes mouse semantics entirely
95	  but you lose `display-menu`'s key shortcuts.
96	
97	The man page (tmux 3.3+) explains why `-O` alone isn't enough:
98	
99	> If the mouse is enabled and the menu is opened from a mouse key binding,
100	> releasing the mouse button … closes the menu. `-M` tells tmux the menu
101	> should handle mouse events; by default only menus opened from mouse key
102	> bindings do so.
103	
104	A submenu launched via `run-shell` is NOT considered "opened from a mouse
105	key binding" — so `-M` doesn't help either, and the trailing mouse events
106	from the now-defunct parent leak into an undefined input state for the
107	child.
108	
109	## Related
110	
111	- `pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md` — different silent failure mode
112	  for the same `display-menu` command (height clamping / menu-too-tall).
113

# Plan: Right-click tab menu — workmux clear + manual bookmark icons

## Context

The tmux right-click tab menu (the one shown in the screenshot — `MouseDown3Status` binding in `dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl` lines 48–80) is currently the default-tmux window menu rendered inline. The user wants two additions:

1. **Clear status** — manually unset `@workmux_status` on the right-clicked window, so a stuck 🤖 / 💬 / ✅ icon (agent killed before its `Stop` hook fired, OOM, terminal crash) can be wiped without typing `wmclear` in the shell or hunting for the workmux sidebar.
2. **Manual bookmark / pin** — let the user tag any tab with one of four icons (⭐ / 📌 / 🔖 / 🚩) that renders **next to** the workmux icon, not in place of it. Clicking the same icon a second time clears it (toggle).

The bookmark layer must not collide with workmux. The repo already exposes the generic `tmux_status_*` API in `dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh` for exactly this use case: it reserves the `workmux*` name prefix and invites other producers to register under `@<name>_status`. We use `@bookmark_status`.

Per the submenu pitfall (`pitfalls/tmux-submenu-flash-and-bottom-right.md`), nested `display-menu` via `run-shell` from a `MouseDown3Status` parent is unreliable — must inline. User has opted to accept menu height growth (+~6 rows).

## Approach

### 1. `dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl` — extend the menu

Insert a new section between `"Rename"` (line 78) and the trailing separator + `"New window"` (lines 79–80). Six new rows + two separators (one before, one after — matches the section pattern used elsewhere in the menu):

\```tmux
"" \
"⭐ Star"     s { run-shell "~/.config/tmux/toggle-bookmark.sh '#{window_id}' '⭐'" } \
"📌 Pin"      p { run-shell "~/.config/tmux/toggle-bookmark.sh '#{window_id}' '📌'" } \
"🔖 Bookmark" b { run-shell "~/.config/tmux/toggle-bookmark.sh '#{window_id}' '🔖'" } \
"🚩 Flag"     f { run-shell "~/.config/tmux/toggle-bookmark.sh '#{window_id}' '🚩'" } \
"Clear agent status" c { set-option -w -t "#{window_id}" -u "@workmux_status" ; display-message "Cleared @workmux_status on #{window_index}:#{window_name}" } \
\```

- `#{window_id}` resolves at menu-display time to the right-clicked window — confirmed by existing `"Rename"` row which uses the same expansion.
- "Clear agent status" inlines `set-option` directly (no `run-shell` needed — keeps it fast).
- The bookmark rows go through a tiny helper script (see #3) because tmux can't easily express "toggle: if current == X, unset; else set to X" in a single `display-menu` command list without nightmare quoting around emoji literals.
- Update the WARNING comment block above the binding (lines 50–60): bump "17 visible rows" → "23 visible rows" and remove the "candidates to drop" hint (user explicitly opted for growth).

### 2. `dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf` — render the bookmark glyph

Append a second conditional to both window-text format strings (lines 31–32). The catppuccin theme already supports chained `#{?@var, …,}` conditionals — line 32 demonstrates the pattern with `window_zoomed_flag`:

Current (line 31):
\```tmux
set -g @catppuccin_window_text ' #W#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}'
\```
New:
\```tmux
set -g @catppuccin_window_text ' #W#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}#{?@bookmark_status, #{@bookmark_status},}'
\```

Current (line 32):
\```tmux
set -g @catppuccin_window_current_text ' #W#{?window_zoomed_flag, 󰊓 ,}#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}'
\```
New:
\```tmux
set -g @catppuccin_window_current_text ' #W#{?window_zoomed_flag, 󰊓 ,}#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}#{?@bookmark_status, #{@bookmark_status},}'
\```

Result: `1: shell 🤖 ⭐` when both are set; `1: shell 🤖` for agent only; `1: shell ⭐` for bookmark only; `1: shell` for neither.

Extend the existing comment block (lines 20–30) to mention the bookmark conditional and link to the toggle helper.

### 3. NEW: `dot_config/tmux/executable_toggle-bookmark.sh` — toggle helper

Deploys as `~/.config/tmux/toggle-bookmark.sh` with `chmod +x`. POSIX `sh`, no zsh-isms.

\```sh
#!/usr/bin/env sh
# Toggle @bookmark_status on a tmux window.
# Usage: toggle-bookmark.sh <window-id> <glyph>
#   If @bookmark_status on <window-id> already equals <glyph>, unset it.
#   Otherwise overwrite it with <glyph>.
# Invoked by the MouseDown3Status menu in dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl.
# Parallels workmux's @workmux_status — independent var, both render side-by-side
# in the catppuccin window-text format.
set -eu

win="${1:-}"
glyph="${2:-}"

if [ -z "$win" ] || [ -z "$glyph" ]; then
    printf 'usage: %s <window-id> <glyph>\n' "$0" >&2
    exit 64
fi

current=$(tmux show-options -wv -t "$win" '@bookmark_status' 2>/dev/null || true)

if [ "$current" = "$glyph" ]; then
    tmux set-option -w -t "$win" -u '@bookmark_status' 2>/dev/null || true
    tmux display-message "Bookmark cleared"
else
    tmux set-option -w -t "$win" '@bookmark_status' "$glyph"
    tmux display-message "Bookmark: $glyph"
fi
\```

No `chezmoi` template — pure shell. The `executable_` prefix gives it `+x` on deploy.

## Files

| Path | Change |
|---|---|
| `dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl` (lines 48–80) | Extend MouseDown3Status menu with 6 new rows + 2 separators; refresh the row-count comment |
| `dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf` (lines 31–32) | Append `#{?@bookmark_status, …,}` conditional to both window-text formats; extend explanatory comment |
| `dot_config/tmux/executable_toggle-bookmark.sh` | **NEW** — POSIX `sh` toggle script |

## Existing utilities reused — do NOT reimplement

- **`tmux_status_*` API** at `dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh`: already validates names, reserves `workmux*` prefix, and provides `tmux_status_set` / `_get` / `_clear` / `_clear_all` / `_list` / `_run`. Users who want to drive `@bookmark_status` from CLI or scripts can do so via this API today (`tmux_status_set bookmark '⭐'`). We do NOT need a shell wrapper or alias for the bookmark — the menu is the front-door UI; the existing helpers are the back door.
- **`wmclear` function** at `dot_config/shell/38_workmux.sh:39–73`: already the canonical CLI escape hatch for clearing `@workmux_status`. We do NOT modify it. The menu's "Clear agent status" row is the GUI equivalent, intentionally narrower (single window only — no `--all` mode in the menu to keep the surface small).
- **`#{window_id}` expansion** in `display-menu`: already used by `Rename` on line 78. Same pattern, no new tmux feature needed.

## Hard rules honored (per CLAUDE.md `workmux` 6-file invariant)

The workmux integration spans 6 files. This plan touches one (`theme.catppuccin.conf`) **additively** — appending a second conditional after the existing `@workmux_status` one. Verified:

1. ✅ `status_format: false` in `dot_config/workmux/config.yaml` — untouched
2. ✅ `command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1` guards in `dot_claude/modify_settings.json` — untouched
3. ✅ `Stop` / `SubagentStop` → `set-window-status done` — untouched
4. ✅ Never runs `workmux setup`
5. ✅ The `@bookmark_status` user-option is reserved by `60_tmux_status.sh`'s validator (rejects `workmux*` names, accepts anything else under `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+`)
6. ✅ Mnemonic letters `s` / `p` / `b` / `f` / `c` don't collide with any existing key in the same `MouseDown3Status` menu (existing: `l r 1 2 3 4 5 m K E X N n w`)

## Cross-file maintenance (per CLAUDE.md)

- **`docs/tools/workmux.md`** — add a one-paragraph note under "Reusing the per-window status mechanism" pointing to the new menu items + the toggle helper. (Read-only mention; the existing API table is already correct.)
- The `dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf` change is a parallel additive line — no need to update the 6-file workmux invariant matrix in `CLAUDE.md` itself (it still spans the same 6 files; we're not adding a 7th surface to the workmux integration, we're using the documented public API).
- **No** alias added to `docs/shells/aliases.md` — we deliberately did not add a shell alias for bookmark toggle; the public `tmux_status_set bookmark <glyph>` already exists and the menu is the front door.

## Verification

1. **Reload tmux config**: `tmux source-file ~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf` (or `prefix + r` if the user has that bound; otherwise restart tmux server with `tmux kill-server` and reattach).
2. **Right-click any tab** → confirm the menu now ends with `⭐ Star`, `📌 Pin`, `🔖 Bookmark`, `🚩 Flag`, `Clear agent status` rows before `New window`.
3. **Toggle bookmark**: right-click tab → `⭐ Star` → confirm `⭐` appears next to the tab name. Right-click same tab → `⭐ Star` again → confirm `⭐` disappears. Right-click → `📌 Pin` → confirm `📌` appears. Right-click → `🔖 Bookmark` → confirm switches from `📌` to `🔖` (overwrite, not toggle, since clicked icon differs from current).
4. **Coexist with workmux**: open Claude Code in a tab so `🤖` appears. Set `⭐` on the same tab → confirm both render: `1: shell 🤖 ⭐`. Click `Clear agent status` → confirm `🤖` disappears but `⭐` remains: `1: shell ⭐`.
5. **Clear from CLI still works**: `wmclear` from a shell in the tab → confirm `🤖` clears (unchanged behavior). `tmux_status_clear bookmark` → confirm `⭐` clears.
6. **Audit per-window vars**: `tmux_status_list` → confirm shows `@workmux_status` and `@bookmark_status` entries with correct glyphs.
7. **Small-terminal check** (height growth: ~23 rows): shrink terminal to ~26 rows tall and right-click a tab → confirm the menu still renders (silent suppression threshold per `pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md`). If suppressed at ≥ 30 rows, revisit and trim.
8. **Mnemonics**: from the open menu, press `s` / `p` / `b` / `f` / `c` directly (without mouse) → confirm each fires its action.

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env sh
# ~/.config/tmux/toggle-bookmark.sh
# Source: dot_config/tmux/executable_toggle-bookmark.sh (managed by chezmoi)
#
# Toggle @bookmark_status on a tmux window. Invoked by the MouseDown3Status
# right-click menu in dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl.
#
# Usage:
#   toggle-bookmark.sh <window-id> <glyph>
#     If @bookmark_status on <window-id> already equals <glyph>, unset it.
#     Otherwise overwrite it with <glyph>.
#
# Parallels workmux's @workmux_status — independent per-window user-option,
# both render side-by-side in the catppuccin window-text format
# (dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf lines 31–32). For CLI access use the
# generic API from dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh:
#   tmux_status_set bookmark '⭐'      # set on current window
#   tmux_status_clear bookmark         # clear on current window
#
# Why this script instead of inlining in display-menu: expressing
# "if current == X then unset else set to X" requires reading the option
# value first, and the quoting around emoji literals inside a nested tmux
# command list (display-menu → { run-shell … } → { set-option … }) is
# fragile. A tiny external script keeps the menu binding readable.

set -eu

win="${1:-}"
glyph="${2:-}"

if [ -z "$win" ] || [ -z "$glyph" ]; then
    printf 'usage: %s <window-id> <glyph>\n' "$0" >&2
    exit 64
fi

current=$(tmux show-options -wv -t "$win" '@bookmark_status' 2>/dev/null || true)

if [ "$current" = "$glyph" ]; then
    tmux set-option -w -t "$win" -u '@bookmark_status' 2>/dev/null || true
    tmux display-message "Bookmark cleared"
else
    tmux set-option -w -t "$win" '@bookmark_status' "$glyph"
    tmux display-message "Bookmark: $glyph"
fi

```

222	## Manual cleanup: `wmclear`
223	
224	```bash
225	# Clear the marker on the current window (calls workmux set-window-status clear)
226	wmclear
227	
228	# Clear marker on a specific window in current session
229	wmclear 5
230	
231	# Nuke every workmux marker in the current tmux session
232	wmclear --all
233	```
234	
235	Implementation lives in `dot_config/zsh/tools/38_workmux.zsh`. The single-
236	window form prefers `workmux set-window-status clear` so workmux's internal
237	agent-state is also reset; the bulk forms fall back to `tmux set-option -w
238	-u @workmux_status` which only clears the user-var.
239	
240	## Sidebar daemon (optional)
241	
242	Run `wm sidebar` (or `wmsb`) once per tmux session to spawn the sidebar
243	pane. Two side benefits beyond the visible status panel:
244	
245	1. **Interrupted-agent detection** — works only while sidebar is running.
246	   Watches each agent pane for output; after 10s of silence on a `working`
247	   agent, marks it interrupted and (per upstream v0.1.163+) downgrades the
248	   icon. Fixes the crash-leak with no manual cleanup.
249	2. **Cross-window status at a glance** — see all running agents and their
250	   git diff stats without `prefix + w`-ing through windows.
251	
252	Cost: one tmux pane (configurable width, default ~30 cols). Auto-resizes
253	on terminal resize. Toggle off with `wm sidebar` again.
254	
255	This repo deliberately does **NOT** auto-spawn the sidebar — too intrusive
256	for users who just want the icons. Add it manually to your tmux startup if
257	you want it everywhere:
258	
259	```bash
260	# Add to your ~/.tmux.conf.local or similar (NOT chezmoi-managed by default)
261	set-hook -g session-created 'run-shell "workmux sidebar 2>/dev/null || true"'
262	```
263	
264	## Adding a new agent
265	
266	Workmux supports Claude, OpenCode, Codex, Copilot CLI, Pi, and Gemini for
267	status tracking ([upstream support
268	matrix](https://workmux.raine.dev/guide/status-tracking#agent-support)).
269	Codex/Copilot/Pi don't have a `waiting` state due to upstream API limits.
270	
271	To add tracking for a new agent **on every machine** (not just one box):
272	
273	1. Read upstream's per-agent setup at
274	   [workmux.raine.dev/guide/status-tracking](https://workmux.raine.dev/guide/status-tracking)
275	   — typically a hook config in the agent's settings file.
276	2. Don't run `wm setup`. Instead vendor the hook config into this repo:
277	   - For agents that already have an overlay file (`dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl`,
278	     etc.), add the hook entries to that overlay's template so the
279	     hook-aware merger preserves user/runtime additions.
280	   - For agents without an overlay yet, model after
281	     [`dot_claude/modify_settings.json`](../../dot_claude/modify_settings.json)
282	     or [`dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts`](../../dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts).
283	3. Wrap the actual `workmux set-window-status` call with
284	   `command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && ... || true` so the hook no-ops
285	   on machines where workmux isn't installed yet.
286	 4. Update the table under [What this repo
287	    manages](#what-this-repo-manages-for-you) with the new file.

301	
302	## Reusing the per-window status mechanism (without workmux)
303	
304	The `@workmux_status` glyph is a thin wrapper over a generic tmux primitive:
305	**per-window user options + a conditional in `window-status-format`**. You
306	can use the same trick for ANY long-running thing whose state you want
307	glanceable in the tab bar — build watchers, test runners, deploy progress,
308	queue depth, alert badges, on-call rotation, anything. Workmux is one
309	producer; you can add more.
310	
311	### The primitive (3 moving parts)
312	
313	1. **Set** a per-window user option (any name starting with `@`):
314	   ```bash
315	   # Current window
316	   tmux set-option -w '@my_status' '🔨'
317	   # Specific window
318	   tmux set-option -w -t 'mysession:3' '@my_status' '⚠️'
319	   # Unset (clear)
320	   tmux set-option -w -u '@my_status'
321	   ```
322	
323	   …or use the **POSIX shell helpers** managed by this repo
324	   ([`dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh`](../../dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh)),
325	   which wrap the raw tmux calls with name validation, list/audit, and
326	   a `run` helper that traps Ctrl+C so badges don't leak. Both zsh and
327	   bash auto-source this file. See the [shell helpers reference
328	   below](#shell-helpers-tmux_status_) for the full API.
329	
330	   ```bash
331	   tmux_status_set my_build 🔨           # tag current window
332	   tmux_status_set my_build 🔨 mysess:3  # tag specific window
333	   tmux_status_clear my_build            # unset (current window)
334	   tmux_status_run my_build 🔨 ✅ ❌ -- npm run build
335	                                         # set 🔨, run cmd, set ✅/❌
336	                                         # by exit code, auto-clear on
337	                                         # signal trap (Ctrl+C safe)
338	   ```
339	
340	2. **Render** it conditionally in `window-status-format` so windows
341	   without the option set don't render anything extra. This repo's
342	   catppuccin theme already appends one such conditional in
343	   [`dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf`](../../dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf):
344	   ```tmux
345	   set -g @catppuccin_window_text ' #W#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}'
346	   ```
347	   To add YOUR badge, append another conditional:
348	   ```tmux
349	   set -g @catppuccin_window_text ' #W#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}#{?@my_status, #{@my_status},}'
350	   ```
351	   Both will coexist (workmux's 🤖 + your 🔨 next to each other when both
352	   are set on the same window).
353	
354	3. **Read** it back to verify or to gate logic:
355	   ```bash
356	   tmux show-options -wv -t 'mysession:3' '@my_status'
357	   tmux list-windows -aF '#{session_name}:#{window_index} marker=#{@my_status}'
358	   ```
359	
360	### When to invent your own user-var vs reuse `@workmux_status`
361	
362	Reuse `@workmux_status` if your status is conceptually "agent-like"
363	(working / waiting / done) — that way `wm sidebar` / `wm dashboard` /
364	`wm last-done` see your producer too, and `wmclear` resets it. Just call
365	`workmux set-window-status working` (or `waiting` / `done` / `clear`)
366	from your hook instead of writing the user-var directly.
367	
368	Invent a new `@<something>_status` user-var when:
369	- The state space differs (e.g. a build watcher with `building` /
370	  `passing` / `failing` is not workmux's working/waiting/done).
371	- You don't want it to appear in `wm dashboard` (workmux only knows
372	  about `@workmux_status`).
373	- Multiple producers should be visible simultaneously (workmux's icon
374	  and your build icon side by side).
375	
376	### Worked example: build watcher
377	
378	The simplest case — wrap any command and get start/success/failure
379	badges with one line, courtesy of `tmux_status_run`:
380	
381	```bash
382	tmux_status_run my_build 🔨 ✅ ❌ -- npm run build
383	```
384	
385	This sets `@my_build_status = 🔨` before the command, swaps to ✅ on
386	exit code 0 or ❌ on non-zero, and traps Ctrl+C / SIGTERM so the badge
387	clears instead of leaking. Wire it into a tmuxinator pre-command, a git
388	hook, a Makefile target, anywhere.
389
```
</details></tool-use>

echo "  state: [$(tmux -L "$SOCK" show-options -wv -t "$WIN" '@bookmark_status' 2>/dev/null || echo unset)]"

echo "  state: [$(tmux -L "$SOCK" show-options -wv -t "$WIN" '@bookmark_status' 2>/dev/null || echo unset)]"

tmux -L "$SOCK" kill-server 2>/dev/null || true
rm -f "$SCRIPT"
